absolut.explanation: "Absolut" means "absolutely". When you want to say "definitely not", put it before "ikke" (not): "absolut ikke" (absolutely not). When you want to say "definitely yes", use it alone: "Kommer du?" "Absolut!" (Are you coming? Absolutely!)

sentence.da: Det er **absolut** umuligt at nå toget nu.
sentence.en: It is absolutely impossible to catch the train now.

abstrakt.explanation: "Abstrakt" means "abstract". When you name a style of art, put it before "kunst": "abstrakt kunst" (abstract art).

sentence.da: Frihed er et **abstrakt** begreb.
sentence.en: Freedom is an abstract concept.

absurd.explanation: "Absurd" means "absurd". When something makes no sense and you want to react, say "Det er absurd!" (That is absurd!)

sentence.da: Det er **absurd**, at en kop kaffe koster tohundrede kroner.
sentence.en: It is absurd that a cup of coffee costs two hundred kroner.

adfærd.explanation: "En adfærd" means "a behavior". Do not mix it up with "en handling" (an action). "Adfærd" is how someone acts in general: "Hundens adfærd er rolig" (The dog's behavior is calm). "En handling" is one act: "Det var en modig handling" (That was a brave act).

sentence.da: Barnets **adfærd** i skolen er blevet bedre.
sentence.en: The child's behavior at school has improved.

adgang.explanation: "Adgang" means "access". To say what you can get into or use, add "til" (to): "Vi har ikke adgang til rummet" (We do not have access to the room).

sentence.da: Med dette kort får du **adgang** til hotellet.
sentence.en: With this card you get access to the hotel.

adopteret.explanation: "Adopteret" means "adopted". It comes from the verb "at adoptere" (to adopt).

sentence.da: Hun er **adopteret** og kom til Danmark som baby.
sentence.en: She is adopted and came to Denmark as a baby.

adskillige.explanation: "Adskillige" means "several". Do not mix it up with "at adskille" (to separate), which starts the same. "Adskillige" goes before a plural noun: "adskillige bøger" (several books). "At adskille" is a verb: "at adskille æg og mel" (to separate eggs and flour).

sentence.da: Der kom **adskillige** gæster til festen.
sentence.en: Several guests came to the party.

adskilt.explanation: "Adskilt" means "separate". Do not mix it up with "skilt" (divorced). "Adskilt" is for things kept apart: "Rummene er adskilt" (The rooms are separate). "Skilt" is for a couple whose marriage has ended: "De er skilt" (They are divorced).

sentence.da: Køkkenet og stuen er **adskilt** af en tynd væg.
sentence.en: The kitchen and the living room are separated by a thin wall.

af og til.explanation: "Af og til" means "now and then". When someone asks how often you do something, you can answer: "Går du i biografen?" "Ja, af og til." (Do you go to the cinema? Yes, now and then.)

forms.da: jeg går i biografen af og til
forms.en: I go to the movie theater now and then

sentence.da: Vi ses ikke ofte, kun **af og til**.
sentence.en: We do not see each other often, only now and then.

afdød.explanation: "Afdød" means "deceased". It is a formal, polite word. When you talk politely about a relative who has died, say "min afdøde far" (my late father).

sentence.da: Min bedstemor er **afdød**, og vi savner hende.
sentence.en: My grandmother is deceased, and we miss her.

affald.explanation: "Affald" means "trash". When you talk about trash in general, leave out "et": "Der er meget affald på gaden" (There is a lot of trash on the street). When you count a bag of it, say the container first: "en pose affald" (a bag of trash).

sentence.da: Vi smider **affald** i skraldespanden.
sentence.en: We throw trash in the trash can.

afgjort.explanation: "Afgjort" means "settled". It comes from the verb "at afgøre" (to decide), so it says that something is decided and certain. Put it before an adjective to mean "definitely": "Den nye bil er afgjort billigere" (The new car is definitely cheaper).

sentence.da: Efter den sidste runde var det **afgjort**, hvem der havde vundet.
sentence.en: After the last round it was decided who had won.

afgørende.explanation: "Afgørende" means "decisive". Do not mix it up with "vigtig" (important). Something "vigtig" matters: "Det er vigtigt at sove" (It is important to sleep). Something "afgørende" decides the result: "et afgørende møde" (a decisive meeting).

sentence.da: Det sidste mål var **afgørende** for, hvem der vandt.
sentence.en: The last goal was decisive for who won.

afhængig.explanation: "Afhængig" means "dependent". When you say what you depend on, add "af" (on): "Barnet er afhængigt af sine forældre" (The child is dependent on its parents). When you mean a habit you cannot stop, it also means "addicted": "Jeg er afhængig af kaffe" (I am addicted to coffee).

sentence.da: Min lillebror er **afhængig** af sin telefon.
sentence.en: My little brother is addicted to his phone.

afhængig af.explanation: "Afhængig af" means "dependent on". It is the adjective "afhængig" (dependent) followed by "af" (on). When you mean a habit you cannot stop, it also means "addicted to": "Han er afhængig af nikotin" (He is addicted to nicotine). When you say that a thing depends on something, use the verb "at afhænge af" (to depend on): "Det afhænger af prisen" (It depends on the price).

sentence.da: En baby er **afhængig af** sine forældre.
sentence.en: A baby is dependent on its parents.

aflyst.explanation: "Aflyst" means "canceled". Do not mix it up with "forsinket" (delayed). A "forsinket" flight still goes: "Flyet er forsinket" (The flight is delayed). An "aflyst" flight does not go at all: "Flyet er aflyst" (The flight is canceled).

sentence.da: Toget er **aflyst** i dag.
sentence.en: The train is canceled today.

afmagt.explanation: "Afmagt" means "powerlessness". It is built from "af" (away from) and "magt" (power). The part "magt" is also in "magtfuld" (powerful): "en magtfuld mand" (a powerful man).

sentence.da: Han følte **afmagt**, da han ikke kunne hjælpe sit barn.
sentence.en: He felt powerless when he could not help his child.

afpresning.explanation: "En afpresning" means "a blackmail case". It comes from the verb "at afpresse" (to blackmail). When you mean the crime in general, leave out "en": "Afpresning er en forbrydelse" (Blackmail is a crime).

sentence.da: Han blev anklaget for **afpresning**, fordi han krævede penge for at tie.
sentence.en: He was accused of blackmail because he demanded money to keep quiet.

afrika.explanation: "Afrika" means "Africa". Spell it with a k, not a c as in English. To name the country at the southern end, put "syd" (south) in front: "Sydafrika" (South Africa).

sentence.da: Løver og elefanter lever i **Afrika**.
sentence.en: Lions and elephants live in Africa.

afrikansk.explanation: "Afrikansk" means "African". It is written with a lowercase letter, while English "African" has a capital. To name a person from Africa, use the noun "en afrikaner" (an African person): "Han er afrikaner" (He is African).

sentence.da: Løven er et **afrikansk** dyr.
sentence.en: The lion is an African animal.

afslappet.explanation: "Afslappet" means "relaxed". It comes from the verb "at slappe af" (to relax). When you describe the feeling of a place, put it before the noun: "en afslappet stemning" (a relaxed mood).

sentence.da: Efter ferien er jeg meget **afslappet**.
sentence.en: After the vacation, I am very relaxed.

afsted.explanation: "Afsted" means "off". When you say you are leaving without naming the place, use it after "skal" (have to): "Vi skal afsted klokken otte" (We are leaving at eight).

sentence.da: Hej hej, jeg skal **afsted** nu.
sentence.en: Bye bye, I have to go now.

aftensmad.explanation: "Aftensmad" means "dinner". It is built from "aften" (evening) and "mad" (food). To ask what is for dinner, say: "Hvad skal vi have til aftensmad?" (What are we having for dinner?)

sentence.da: Om aftenen spiser vi **aftensmad** sammen.
sentence.en: In the evening we eat dinner together.

afvænning.explanation: "Afvænning" means "rehab or detox". It is built from "af" (off) and "at vænne" (to accustom). The same verb is in "at vænne sig til" (to get used to): "Jeg skal vænne mig til kulden" (I have to get used to the cold).

sentence.da: Efter flere år med alkohol startede han på **afvænning**.
sentence.en: After several years with alcohol, he started rehab.

aggressiv.explanation: "Aggressiv" means "aggressive". When you describe how someone speaks, say "en aggressiv tone" (an aggressive tone): "Hun talte i en aggressiv tone" (She spoke in an aggressive tone).

sentence.da: Hunden er **aggressiv** og viser tænderne.
sentence.en: The dog is aggressive and shows its teeth.

akademisk.explanation: "Akademisk" means "academic". To name a person with a university degree, use the noun "en akademiker" (a person with a university degree): "Min søster er akademiker" (My sister has a university degree).

sentence.da: Hun har taget en **akademisk** uddannelse på universitetet.
sentence.en: She has completed an academic education at the university.

akavet.explanation: "Akavet" means "awkward". When a moment feels uncomfortable, you can say "Det er lidt akavet" (That is a bit awkward).

sentence.da: Det blev **akavet**, da ingen sagde noget.
sentence.en: It got awkward when nobody said anything.

aktiv.explanation: "Aktiv" means "active". When you say what a person takes part in, add "i" (in): "Han er meget aktiv i klubben" (He is very active in the club). When you talk about an account that is turned on, it also means "active": "Din konto er aktiv" (Your account is active).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er stadig meget **aktiv** og går lange ture.
sentence.en: My grandfather is still very active and takes long walks.

aktuel.explanation: "Aktuel" means "current". Do not mix it up with "faktisk" (actually), even though English "actual" looks similar. "Aktuel" is about what matters now: "de aktuelle priser" (the current prices). "Faktisk" means "in fact": "Jeg er faktisk træt" (I am actually tired).

sentence.da: Debatten om huspriserne er meget **aktuel** lige nu.
sentence.en: The debate about house prices is very topical right now.

akut.explanation: "Akut" means "urgent". It is built into "en akutmodtagelse" (an emergency room), made from "akut" and "modtagelse" (reception): "Hun kom på akutmodtagelsen" (She came to the emergency room).

sentence.da: Hvis det er **akut**, skal du ringe til 112.
sentence.en: If it is urgent, you must call 112.

al.explanation: "Al" means "all". When you talk about an en-word with "the" on the end, use "al": "al musikken" (all the music). Before an et-word, use "alt" (all) instead: "alt arbejdet" (all the work).

sentence.da: Jeg har spist **al** maden.
sentence.en: I have eaten all the food.

aldeles.explanation: "Aldeles" means "quite". When you want to make a describing word stronger, put it before the word: "aldeles ubrugelig" (entirely useless).

sentence.da: Din idé er **aldeles** genial.
sentence.en: Your idea is quite brilliant.

aldrig.explanation: "Aldrig" means "never". It already says "not", so do not add "ikke" (not): "Jeg drikker aldrig kaffe" (I never drink coffee).

sentence.da: Hun spiser **aldrig** kød.
sentence.en: She never eats meat.

alene.explanation: "Alene" means "alone". Do not mix it up with "ensom" (lonely). "Alene" only says nobody else is there: "Jeg går en tur alene" (I go for a walk alone). "Ensom" is a feeling: "Jeg føler mig ensom" (I feel lonely).

sentence.da: Ingen er hjemme. Jeg er **alene**.
sentence.en: Nobody is home. I am alone.

alkohol.explanation: "Alkohol" means "alcohol". When you talk about alcohol in general, leave out "en": "Jeg drikker ikke alkohol" (I do not drink alcohol). The ending "-fri" (free) makes "alkoholfri øl" (alcohol-free beer).

sentence.da: Der er **alkohol** i øl og vin.
sentence.en: There is alcohol in beer and wine.

alle.explanation: "Alle" means "everyone". Do not mix it up with "alt" (everything). "Alle" is for people: "Alle er glade" (Everyone is happy). "Alt" is for things: "Alt er klart" (Everything is ready).

sentence.da: **Alle** børn er hjemme i dag.
sentence.en: All the children are home today.

allerede.explanation: "Allerede" means "already". When something is true sooner than you thought, use it: "Han er allerede her" (He is already here). When the sentence has "ikke" (not), use "endnu" (yet) instead: "Han er her ikke endnu" (He is not here yet).

sentence.da: Maden er **allerede** klar.
sentence.en: The food is ready already.

allergisk.explanation: "Allergisk" means "allergic". To say what causes your allergy, add "over for" (to): "Jeg er allergisk over for nødder" (I am allergic to nuts).

sentence.da: Han er **allergisk** og kan ikke spise æg.
sentence.en: He is allergic and cannot eat eggs.

alligevel.explanation: "Alligevel" means "anyway". When something happens despite a problem, add it: "Det regner, men vi går alligevel" (It is raining, but we are going anyway).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt, men jeg kommer **alligevel**.
sentence.en: I am tired, but I am coming anyway.

almindelig.explanation: "Almindelig" means "ordinary". When you say a mistake is one that happens to many people, it means "common": "Det er en almindelig fejl" (It is a common mistake).

sentence.da: Det var bare en **almindelig** dag på arbejde.
sentence.en: It was just an ordinary day at work.

almægtig.explanation: "Almægtig" means "almighty". It is built from "al" (all) and "mægtig" (mighty). When you name God, the phrase is "Gud den almægtige" (God the Almighty).

sentence.da: Mange tror på en **almægtig** gud, der har skabt verden.
sentence.en: Many believe in an almighty god who created the world.

alt.explanation: "Alt" means "everything". Do not mix it up with "alle" (everyone): "Alt er her" (Everything is here) and "Alle er her" (Everyone is here). To say "far too", put "for" after it: "alt for dyrt" (far too expensive).

sentence.da: Jeg har glemt **alt**.
sentence.en: I have forgotten everything.

alt i alt.explanation: "Alt i alt" means "all in all". When you sum up a story, start with it: "Alt i alt var det en god dag" (All in all it was a good day).

forms.da: Alt i alt går det godt.
forms.en: All in all it is going well.

sentence.da: **Alt i alt** var rejsen rigtig god.
sentence.en: All in all the trip was really good.

alternativ.explanation: "Alternativ" means "alternative". When you talk about something outside the mainstream, it also fits: "alternativ medicin" (alternative medicine).

sentence.da: Vi har brug for en **alternativ** plan, hvis det regner.
sentence.en: We need an alternative plan if it rains.

altid.explanation: "Altid" means "always". It is built from "al" (all) and "tid" (time): "Jeg er altid træt" (I am always tired).

sentence.da: Jeg står **altid** op klokken seks.
sentence.en: I always get up at six o'clock.

alting.explanation: "Alting" means "everything". It is built from "al" (all) and "ting" (things). To say "not everything", put "ikke" (not) before it: "Ikke alting er dyrt" (Not everything is expensive).

sentence.da: Hun ved **alting** om heste.
sentence.en: She knows everything about horses.

altså.explanation: "Altså" means "so". When you sum up what was just said, use it: "Han er syg, så han kommer altså ikke" (He is sick, so he is not coming). When you want to stress a point, it works like "really": "Det er altså dyrt!" (It really is expensive!)

sentence.da: Nu skal du **altså** gå i seng!
sentence.en: Now you really have to go to bed!

aluminium.explanation: "Aluminium" means "aluminum". Spell it with "ium" at the end, as in British English "aluminium". When you say what something is made of, use "af" (of) and no article: "Vinduerne er af aluminium" (The windows are made of aluminum).

sentence.da: Sodavandsdåser er lavet af **aluminium**, fordi det er let.
sentence.en: Soda cans are made of aluminum because it is light.

alverden.explanation: "Alverden" means "the whole wide world". It is built from "al" (all) and "verden" (world). When you add an s and put it before a noun, it means "all kinds of": "alverdens mad" (all kinds of food).

sentence.da: Pizzaen er kendt af **alverden**.
sentence.en: Pizza is known by the whole world.

alvor.explanation: "Alvor" means "serious". When you ask whether someone means it, say "Er det dit alvor?" (Are you serious?). When the fun is over, say "Nu er det alvor" (Now it is serious).

sentence.da: Jeg mener det i fuldt **alvor**.
sentence.en: I mean it in all seriousness.

alvorlig.explanation: "Alvorlig" means "serious". When you talk about something that is a real worry, put it before the noun: "et alvorligt uheld" (a serious accident). When you describe a person who does not joke around, it also works: "Han er meget alvorlig" (He is very serious).

sentence.da: Lægen siger, at det er en **alvorlig** sygdom.
sentence.en: The doctor says that it is a serious illness.

ambitiøs.explanation: "Ambitiøs" means "ambitious". Spell it with "ø", ending "-iøs", where English has "-ious". It comes from the noun "en ambition" (an ambition).

sentence.da: Hun er **ambitiøs** og vil være chef en dag.
sentence.en: She is ambitious and wants to be a boss one day.

amerikansk.explanation: "Amerikansk" means "American". It is written with a lowercase letter, while English "American" has a capital. When you name the sport, say "amerikansk fodbold" (American football).

sentence.da: Burgere er **amerikansk** mad.
sentence.en: Burgers are American food.

ammunition.explanation: "Ammunition" means "ammunition". When you talk about ammunition in general, leave out the article: "Vi har ikke mere ammunition" (We have no more ammunition). When you mean facts that help you win an argument, it also works: "Det giver hende ammunition" (That gives her ammunition).

sentence.da: Jægeren køber **ammunition**, fordi han skal ud at skyde.
sentence.en: The hunter buys ammunition because he is going out to shoot.

anden.explanation: "Anden" means "second". When you count in order (first, second, third) and the word is an en-word, use "anden": "min anden dag" (my second day). With an et-word, use "andet": "det andet barn" (the second child). When you point to the other one of two things, it means "other": "den anden bil" (the other car). In a list, "den anden bil" can also mean "the second car", so the sentence around it tells you which.

sentence.da: I dag er min **anden** dag her.
sentence.en: Today is my second day here.

anderledes.explanation: "Anderledes" means "different". Do not mix it up with "forskellig" (different). "Anderledes" compares something with what you know: "Det smager anderledes" (It tastes different). "Forskellig" is for two or more things that are not alike: "De er forskellige" (They are different).

sentence.da: Min nye skole er helt **anderledes**, ikke som den gamle.
sentence.en: My new school is completely different, not like the old one.

anger.explanation: "Anger" means "remorse". It looks like the English word "anger", but it means something else. For anger, Danes say "vrede": "Han var fuld af vrede" (He was full of anger). For remorse, say "anger": "Jeg føler anger over det, jeg sagde" (I feel remorse about what I said).

sentence.da: Han følte **anger** over, at han havde løjet for sin ven.
sentence.en: He felt remorse that he had lied to his friend.

angst.explanation: "Angst" means "anxiety". To name a sudden attack of it, use "et angstanfald" (an anxiety attack): "Han fik et angstanfald" (He had an anxiety attack).

sentence.da: Han har **angst** for at tale foran folk.
sentence.en: He has anxiety about speaking in front of people.

angående.explanation: "Angående" means "concerning". Put the topic right after it: "Angående ferien" (Concerning the vacation). It sounds formal, so in everyday talk say "om" (about): "Vi taler om ferien" (We are talking about the vacation).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver til dig **angående** din regning.
sentence.en: I am writing to you concerning your bill.

anonym.explanation: "Anonym" means "anonymous". Danish leaves off the ending "-ous" that English has. When you name the group for people who want to stop drinking, Danes say "Anonyme Alkoholikere" (Alcoholics Anonymous).

sentence.da: Pengene kom fra en **anonym** giver, som ingen kender.
sentence.en: The money came from an anonymous donor whom nobody knows.

anonymt.explanation: "Anonymt" means "anonymously". Do not mix it up with "anonym" (anonymous). "Anonym" goes with a noun: "en anonym giver" (an anonymous donor). "Anonymt" says how someone does an action: "Han giver anonymt" (He gives anonymously). "Anonymt" is also the form with an et-word: "et anonymt brev" (an anonymous letter).

forms.en: She wrote anonymously to the newspaper

sentence.da: Hun gav pengene til skolen **anonymt**, uden at nævne sit navn.
sentence.en: She gave the money to the school anonymously, without mentioning her name.

anspændt.explanation: "Anspændt" means "tense". Do not mix it up with "spændt" (excited). "Anspændt" is a strained feeling: "en anspændt nakke" (a tense neck). "Spændt" is looking forward to something: "Jeg er spændt på filmen" (I am excited about the movie).

sentence.da: Stemningen var **anspændt**, og ingen turde sige noget.
sentence.en: The atmosphere was tense, and nobody dared to say anything.

anstrengende.explanation: "Anstrengende" means "tiring". Do not mix it up with "træt" (tired). "Anstrengende" describes what causes it: "Arbejdet er anstrengende" (The work is tiring). "Træt" describes you: "Jeg er træt" (I am tired).

sentence.da: Det er **anstrengende** at gå op ad bakken med tung oppakning.
sentence.en: It is tiring to walk up the hill with heavy luggage.

anstændig.explanation: "Anstændig" means "decent". When you describe an honest, respectful person, use it for the person: "En anstændig chef lytter" (A decent boss listens). When you describe something that is good enough, use it for the thing: "Det var et anstændigt resultat" (That was a decent result).

sentence.da: Han er en **anstændig** mand og siger altid sandheden.
sentence.en: He is a decent man and always tells the truth.

ansvarlig.explanation: "Ansvarlig" means "responsible". When you ask who is in charge, say "Hvem er ansvarlig?" (Who is in charge?). To say what you are responsible for, add "for": "Jeg er ansvarlig for kassen" (I am responsible for the cash register).

sentence.da: Hun er **ansvarlig** og passer godt på sin lillebror.
sentence.en: She is responsible and takes good care of her little brother.

ansvarsfuld.explanation: "Ansvarsfuld" means "responsible". Do not mix it up with "ansvarlig" (responsible). "Ansvarsfuld" is for careful, thoughtful behavior: "ansvarsfuld adfærd" (responsible behavior). "Ansvarlig" is for being in charge or to blame: "Han er ansvarlig for ulykken" (He is responsible for the accident).

sentence.da: En **ansvarsfuld** chauffør kører langsomt, når vejen er glat.
sentence.en: A responsible driver drives slowly when the road is slippery.

antarktis.explanation: "Antarktis" means "Antarctica". Do not mix it up with "Arktis" (the Arctic) in the north. When you say where penguins live, say "Pingviner bor i Antarktis" (Penguins live in Antarctica). When you say where polar bears live, say "Isbjørne bor i Arktis" (Polar bears live in the Arctic).

sentence.da: Næsten hele **Antarktis** er dækket af is.
sentence.en: Almost all of Antarctica is covered in ice.

antibiotika.explanation: "Antibiotika" means "antibiotics". When you talk about taking it, use no article: "Hun får antibiotika" (She is getting antibiotics). To name resistance to it, add "resistens": "antibiotikaresistens" (antibiotic resistance).

sentence.da: Lægen giver mig **antibiotika** mod infektionen.
sentence.en: The doctor gives me antibiotics for the infection.

anvendelig.explanation: "Anvendelig" means "usable". It comes from the verb "at anvende" (to use). To say where it works, add "i" (in): "anvendelig i praksis" (usable in practice).

sentence.da: Den nye metode er meget **anvendelig** i det daglige arbejde.
sentence.en: The new method is very usable in everyday work.

appelsinjuice.explanation: "Appelsinjuice" means "orange juice". It is built from "appelsin" (orange) and "juice" (juice). To name another juice, put the fruit in front of "juice": "æblejuice" (apple juice).

sentence.da: **Appelsinjuice** er en sød drik lavet af appelsiner.
sentence.en: Orange juice is a sweet drink made from oranges.

appetit.explanation: "Appetit" means "appetite". Do not mix it up with "lyst" (a wish to do something). "Appetit" is for food: "Jeg har ingen appetit" (I have no appetite). "At have lyst til" is for doing something: "Jeg har lyst til at gå en tur" (I feel like going for a walk).

sentence.da: Efter turen havde vi stor **appetit**.
sentence.en: After the trip we had a big appetite.

april.explanation: "April" means "April". Write it with a lowercase letter, where English has a capital: "i april" (in April). To say "April fool", join it with "nar" (fool): "aprilsnar" (April fool).

sentence.da: Efter marts kommer **april**.
sentence.en: After March comes April.

arabisk.explanation: "Arabisk" means "Arabic". It is written with a lowercase letter, while English "Arabic" has a capital. To name a language, use it alone: "Hun taler arabisk" (She speaks Arabic).

sentence.da: Hun kommer fra Egypten og taler **arabisk**.
sentence.en: She comes from Egypt and speaks Arabic.

arbejdskraft.explanation: "Arbejdskraft" means "labor". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "kraft" (power): "Vi har brug for mere arbejdskraft" (We need more labor). When you mean the workers themselves, use the plural "arbejdskræfter": "udenlandske arbejdskræfter" (foreign workers).

sentence.da: Landet mangler **arbejdskraft**, fordi mange er gået på pension.
sentence.en: The country lacks labor because many have retired.

arbejdsløs.explanation: "Arbejdsløs" means "unemployed". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "løs" (without). The same "løs" is in "hjemløs" (homeless): "en hjemløs kat" (a homeless cat).

sentence.da: Han har været **arbejdsløs** i tre måneder.
sentence.en: He has been unemployed for three months.

arbejdsløshed.explanation: "Arbejdsløshed" means "unemployment". It is built from "arbejde" (work), "løs" (without) and the ending "-hed", which makes a noun: "sikker" (safe) becomes "sikkerhed" (safety).

sentence.da: Når fabrikken lukker, bliver der mere **arbejdsløshed** i byen.
sentence.en: When the factory closes, there is more unemployment in the town.

arbejdstid.explanation: "En arbejdstid" means "working hours". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "tid" (time). When you mean outside those hours, say "uden for arbejdstid" (outside working hours).

sentence.da: Min **arbejdstid** begynder klokken otte og slutter klokken seksten.
sentence.en: My working hours start at eight and end at four in the afternoon.

arkitektur.explanation: "En arkitektur" means "architecture". It is built on "en arkitekt" (an architect). When you talk about how a computer system is organized, use "it-arkitektur" (IT architecture).

sentence.da: Husene, kirkerne og broerne i en by udgør dens **arkitektur**.
sentence.en: The houses, churches and bridges in a city make up its architecture.

arrogant.explanation: "Arrogant" means "arrogant". Do not mix it up with "stolt" (proud). "Arrogant" is about how you treat other people: "Chefen er arrogant" (The boss is arrogant). "Stolt" is about feeling good about something: "Jeg er stolt af dig" (I am proud of you).

sentence.da: Han ser ned på alle og er meget **arrogant**.
sentence.en: He looks down on everyone and is very arrogant.

asiatisk.explanation: "Asiatisk" means "Asian". It is written with a lowercase letter, while English "Asian" has a capital. To name a person from Asia, use the noun "en asiat" (an Asian person): "Han er asiat" (He is Asian).

sentence.da: Kina er et **asiatisk** land.
sentence.en: China is an Asian country.

asien.explanation: "Asien" means "Asia". Spell it with "-ien" at the end, not "-ia" as in English. The adjective is "asiatisk" (Asian): "asiatisk mad" (Asian food).

sentence.da: Kina og Japan ligger i **Asien**.
sentence.en: China and Japan are in Asia.

aske.explanation: "Aske" means "ash". It is the first part of "et askebæger" (an ashtray). The day that starts Lent is called "Askeonsdag" (Ash Wednesday).

sentence.da: Efter branden var der kun **aske** tilbage i pejsen.
sentence.en: After the fire there was only ash left in the fireplace.

assistance.explanation: "Assistance" means "assistance". It sounds more formal than "hjælp" (help). A shop worker may ask "Kan jeg være til assistance?" (Can I be of assistance?). Between friends, say "Skal jeg hjælpe dig?" (Shall I help you?)

sentence.da: Kan jeg få **assistance** ved kassen?
sentence.en: Can I get assistance at the checkout?

astma.explanation: "Astma" means "asthma". When you say you have it, leave out "en": "Jeg har astma" (I have asthma). A sudden attack is "et astmaanfald", built from "astma" and "anfald" (attack).

sentence.da: Når man har **astma**, bliver det svært at trække vejret.
sentence.en: When you have asthma, it becomes hard to breathe.

at acceptere.explanation: "At acceptere" means "to accept". When you agree to an offer, say "Jeg accepterer dit tilbud" (I accept your offer). When you say you cannot live with a situation, use "ikke": "Hun kan ikke acceptere, at han kommer for sent" (She cannot accept that he is late).

sentence.da: Du kan **acceptere** eller sige nej til jobbet.
sentence.en: You can accept or say no to the job.

at adlyde.explanation: "At adlyde" means "to obey". It takes its object directly, with no small word after it: "at adlyde en ordre" (to obey an order).

sentence.da: Børn skal **adlyde** deres forældre, når de er små.
sentence.en: Children must obey their parents when they are small.

at adskille.explanation: "At adskille" means "to separate". Do not mix it up with "at skille" (to separate a couple). "At adskille" is for pulling things apart: "at adskille børnene" (to separate the children). "At skille" is for ending a marriage: "De blev skilt" (They got divorced).

sentence.da: Vi må **adskille** hundene, fordi de bliver ved med at slås.
sentence.en: We must separate the dogs because they keep fighting.

at advare.explanation: "At advare" means "to warn". To say what the danger is, add "mod" (against): "Jeg advarer dig mod hunden" (I am warning you about the dog).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **advare** dig mod den glatte vej.
sentence.en: I want to warn you about the slippery road.

at afbestille.explanation: "At afbestille" means "to cancel (an order or booking)". Do not mix it up with "at aflyse" (to call off). "At afbestille" is for something you booked: "Jeg afbestiller hotelværelset" (I cancel the hotel room). "At aflyse" is for an event: "Vi aflyser festen" (We call off the party).

forms.en: I have canceled (an order or booking)

sentence.da: Vi må **afbestille** bordet, fordi Anna er syg.
sentence.en: We have to cancel the table because Anna is sick.

at afbryde.explanation: "At afbryde" means "to interrupt". When you want to speak up politely, say "Undskyld, jeg afbryder" (Sorry to interrupt). When you stop a connection or the power, it also means "to cut off": "at afbryde forbindelsen" (to cut off the connection).

sentence.da: Det er uhøfligt at **afbryde** folk, når de taler.
sentence.en: It is rude to interrupt people when they are speaking.

at afbøde.explanation: "At afbøde" means "to mitigate". When you reduce damage after it has happened, use it: "at afbøde skaderne" (to soften the damage). Do not mix it up with "at afværge" (to avert), which stops it before it happens: "at afværge en ulykke" (to avert an accident).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **afbøde** virkningerne af oversvømmelsen med nye diger.
sentence.en: The municipality will mitigate the effects of the flood with new dikes.

at affyre.explanation: "At affyre" means "to fire (a weapon)". Do not mix it up with "at fyre" (to fire someone from a job). "At affyre" is for a weapon: "at affyre en raket" (to fire a rocket). "At fyre" is for a worker: "Chefen fyrer ham" (The boss fires him).

sentence.da: Soldaten må kun **affyre** våbnet, når han får ordre.
sentence.en: The soldier may only fire the weapon when he gets an order.

at afgive.explanation: "At afgive" means "to give off or submit". When a thing sends out heat or a smell, it means "give off": "afgive varme" (give off heat). When a person makes a formal statement, it means "submit": "afgive et løfte" (make a promise).

sentence.da: Når du er atten, kan du **afgive** din stemme ved valget.
sentence.en: When you are eighteen, you can cast your vote in the election.

at afgå.explanation: "At afgå" means "to depart". When a train, bus or ferry leaves at a set time, it uses this verb: "Færgen afgår klokken otte" (The ferry departs at eight). When someone gives up a position, it means "to step down": "afgå som formand" (step down as chair).

sentence.da: Toget skal **afgå** klokken ti fra spor tre.
sentence.en: The train is to depart at ten from platform three.

at afgøre.explanation: "At afgøre" means "to decide or settle". When something open gets an answer, such as a match: "Straffesparket afgjorde kampen" (The penalty kick decided the match). Do not mix it up with "at beslutte" (to decide). "At beslutte" is for your own plan: "Jeg har besluttet at flytte" (I have decided to move).

sentence.da: Dommeren skal **afgøre**, hvem der har ret i sagen.
sentence.en: The judge must decide who is right in the case.

at afhente.explanation: "At afhente" means "to collect or pick up". It is for something that is waiting for you: "at afhente bestillingen" (to collect the order). Do not mix it up with "at hente" (to fetch), which also works for a person: "Jeg henter dig klokken fem" (I will pick you up at five).

sentence.da: Du kan **afhente** pakken på posthuset efter klokken to.
sentence.en: You can collect the package at the post office after two o'clock.

at afholde.explanation: "At afholde" means "to hold (an event)". It is for something planned: "at afholde valg" (to hold an election). Do not mix it up with "at holde" (to hold in your hand): "Jeg holder en kop" (I am holding a cup). With "sig fra" (yourself from) it means "to refrain from": "at afholde sig fra sukker" (to stay away from sugar).

sentence.da: Skolen vil **afholde** et forældremøde i næste uge.
sentence.en: The school will hold a parents' meeting next week.

at afhænge af.explanation: "At afhænge af" means "to depend on": "Det afhænger af vejret" (It depends on the weather). Another way to say "it depends" is "det kommer an på": "Det kommer an på prisen" (It depends on the price).

sentence.da: Prisen vil **afhænge af** størrelsen.
sentence.en: The price will depend on the size.

at afhøre.explanation: "At afhøre" means "to interrogate". When you only want to ask an ordinary question, use "at spørge" (to ask) instead: "Jeg spørger om vejen" (I am asking about the way).

sentence.da: Politiet vil **afhøre** manden, fordi han så ulykken.
sentence.en: The police will interrogate the man because he saw the accident.

at afkræfte.explanation: "At afkræfte" means "to disprove". When you show that a claim is wrong: "Testen afkræfter rygtet" (The test disproves the rumor). Do not mix it up with "at bekræfte" (to confirm): "Testen bekræfter rygtet" (The test confirms the rumor).

sentence.da: Nye tests kan **afkræfte** den gamle teori.
sentence.en: New tests can disprove the old theory.

at afkøle.explanation: "At afkøle" means "to cool (something) down". To tell someone to let food get cooler, say: "Lad kagen afkøle" (Let the cake cool).

sentence.da: Is kan hurtigt **afkøle** en varm drik.
sentence.en: Ice can quickly cool a hot drink.

at aflaste.explanation: "At aflaste" means "to relieve", as in taking work or weight off someone. It is built from "af" (off) and "en last" (a load).

sentence.da: Min bror vil **aflaste** mig ved at passe børnene i weekenden.
sentence.en: My brother will relieve me by looking after the children on the weekend.

at aflevere.explanation: "At aflevere" means "to hand in or deliver". To say you leave your children at school, use it for dropping someone off: "Jeg afleverer børnene i skole" (I drop the children off at school).

sentence.da: Du skal **aflevere** rapporten før fredag.
sentence.en: You have to hand in the report before Friday.

at aflyse.explanation: "At aflyse" means "to cancel". To say an event will not happen, use it for the event: "Koncerten er aflyst" (The concert is canceled). To cancel something you booked yourself, use "at afbestille" (to cancel an order): "Jeg vil gerne afbestille bordet" (I would like to cancel the table).

sentence.da: De må **aflyse** mødet på grund af sne.
sentence.en: They have to cancel the meeting because of snow.

at aflægge.explanation: "At aflægge" means "to pay (a visit) or take (an oath)". To say you visit someone, use "besøg" (visit) after it: "at aflægge besøg" (to pay a visit). To say you swear in court, use "ed" (oath) after it: "at aflægge ed" (to take an oath). To put something down, use "at lægge" (to put): "Jeg lægger bogen på bordet" (I put the book on the table).

forms.en: I have paid (a visit) / taken (an oath)

sentence.da: Vidnet skal **aflægge** ed, før hun må forklare sig i retten.
sentence.en: The witness must take an oath before she may give her statement in court.

at afmelde.explanation: "At afmelde" means "to cancel or unsubscribe". To say you take yourself off a course, add "sig" (yourself) and "fra" (from): "Jeg afmelder mig fra kurset" (I cancel my place on the course).

sentence.da: Du kan **afmelde** nyhedsbrevet nederst i mailen.
sentence.en: You can unsubscribe from the newsletter at the bottom of the email.

at afmontere.explanation: "At afmontere" means "to dismantle". It is built from "af" (off) and "at montere" (to install), so it is the opposite: you take off what was installed.

sentence.da: Vi skal **afmontere** lampen, før vi kan male loftet.
sentence.en: We must remove the lamp before we can paint the ceiling.

at afprøve.explanation: "At afprøve" means "to test or try out". It comes from the verb "at prøve" (to try). To say you try something new, put it after the verb: "at afprøve en ny opskrift" (to try out a new recipe).

sentence.da: Vi vil **afprøve** den nye metode på en lille gruppe.
sentence.en: We want to try out the new method on a small group.

at afsende.explanation: "At afsende" means "to send or dispatch". It comes from the verb "at sende" (to send). The person who sends something is "en afsender" (a sender).

sentence.da: Butikken skal **afsende** alle ordrer, før posthuset lukker.
sentence.en: The shop must send out all orders before the post office closes.

at afskaffe.explanation: "At afskaffe" means "to abolish". To say a new rule is brought in, use the opposite, "at indføre" (to introduce): "De vil indføre en ny skat" (They want to introduce a new tax).

sentence.da: Regeringen vil **afskaffe** skatten på gamle biler.
sentence.en: The government wants to abolish the tax on old cars.

at afslutte.explanation: "At afslutte" means "to finish or end". To say you end something yourself, put the thing after it: "Jeg afslutter mødet" (I end the meeting). To say something ends by itself, use "at slutte" (to end): "Filmen slutter nu" (The movie ends now).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **afslutte** rapporten i dag.
sentence.en: I have to finish the report today.

at afslå.explanation: "At afslå" means "to decline or refuse". To say an office turns down an application, use it for the answer: "Kommunen afslog ansøgningen" (The municipality turned down the application). To say no politely to an invitation, use "at takke nej" (to say no thanks): "Jeg takker nej til invitationen" (I say no thanks to the invitation).

sentence.da: Banken vil **afslå** lånet, fordi hun ikke har noget arbejde.
sentence.en: The bank will decline the loan because she has no job.

at afsløre.explanation: "At afsløre" means "to reveal". To say something secret comes out, use it for the secret: "Avisen afslørede planen" (The newspaper revealed the plan). To say someone is caught doing something wrong, use it for the person: "Politiet afslørede tyven" (The police caught the thief).

sentence.da: Avisen vil **afsløre**, hvem der står bag svindlen.
sentence.en: The newspaper wants to expose who is behind the fraud.

at afspejle.explanation: "At afspejle" means "to reflect", as in a mirror or water sending back an image. When something shows what is true, it also means "to reflect": "Valget afspejler, hvad folk mener" (The election reflects what people think). To say you think something over, use "at tænke over" (to think about): "Jeg tænker over dit tilbud" (I am thinking about your offer).

sentence.da: Vandet kan **afspejle** træerne, når det er helt stille.
sentence.en: The water can reflect the trees when it is completely still.

at afstå.explanation: "At afstå" means "to give up or refrain". To say someone gives up something that belongs to them, use it for the right: "Han afstår sin ret til arven" (He gives up his right to the inheritance).

sentence.da: Han vil **afstå** fra at drikke kaffe efter klokken fire.
sentence.en: He will refrain from drinking coffee after four o'clock.

at afsætte.explanation: "At afsætte" means "to set aside or sell". To say money is set aside for a purpose, use it for the money: "Kommunen afsætter penge til en ny skole" (The municipality sets aside money for a new school). To talk about selling goods, say "at afsætte varer" (to sell goods).

sentence.da: Vi skal **afsætte** to timer til mødet i morgen.
sentence.en: We must set aside two hours for the meeting tomorrow.

at aftage.explanation: "At aftage" means "to decrease". It is built from "af" (off) and "at tage" (to take).

sentence.da: Smerten vil **aftage**, når medicinen begynder at virke.
sentence.en: The pain will ease when the medicine starts to work.

at aftale.explanation: "At aftale" means "to agree or arrange". The thing you agree on is called "en aftale" (an agreement). To say you have a meeting booked, say: "Jeg har en aftale klokken ti" (I have an appointment at ten o'clock).

sentence.da: Vi skal **aftale** en tid for mødet.
sentence.en: We have to arrange a time for the meeting.

at afvente.explanation: "At afvente" means "to await". To say you wait for an answer with this word, put the answer right after it, with no small word between: "afvente svar" (await an answer). The shorter "at vente" (to wait) needs "på" (for): "vente på svar" (wait for an answer).

sentence.da: Vi må **afvente** lægens svar, før vi kan gøre mere.
sentence.en: We must await the doctor's answer before we can do more.

at afvise.explanation: "At afvise" means "to reject". To say you refuse to do something yourself, use "at nægte" (to refuse): "Han nægtede at betale" (He refused to pay).

sentence.da: Banken vil **afvise** ansøgningen, hvis papirerne ikke er i orden.
sentence.en: The bank will reject the application if the papers are not in order.

at afværge.explanation: "At afværge" means "to avert". To say you make something that has already happened less bad, use "at afbøde" (to mitigate): "Vi forsøger at afbøde skaden" (We are trying to limit the damage).

sentence.da: Hun greb ind for at **afværge** et slagsmål.
sentence.en: She stepped in to avert a fight.

at agere.explanation: "At agere" means "to act", as in playing a role or behaving in a certain way. To say you react to something, use "at reagere" (to react): "Jeg reagerer på lyden" (I react to the sound).

sentence.da: Skuespilleren kan **agere** vred uden at sige et ord.
sentence.en: The actor can act angry without saying a word.

at analysere.explanation: "At analysere" means "to analyze". To say what you study closely, put the thing after the verb: "Vi analyserer resultaterne" (We analyze the results).

sentence.da: Laboratoriet skal **analysere** blodprøven og finde årsagen.
sentence.en: The lab must analyze the blood sample and find the cause.

at anbefale.explanation: "At anbefale" means "to recommend". To say what a doctor advises, use it for the advice: "Lægen anbefaler hvile" (The doctor recommends rest).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **anbefale** denne gode bog til dig.
sentence.en: I would like to recommend this good book to you.

at anbringe.explanation: "At anbringe" means "to place". To say you put something in a chosen spot, say: "at anbringe en kasse" (to place a box). To talk about a child placed in care, use the describing form: "et anbragt barn" (a child placed in care).

sentence.da: Kommunen kan **anbringe** barnet hos en plejefamilie.
sentence.en: The municipality can place the child with a foster family.

at ane.explanation: "At ane" means "to have an idea or suspect". To say you have no idea, say: "Jeg aner det ikke" (I have no idea).

forms.en: I have had an idea / suspected

sentence.da: Hun må ikke **ane**, at vi planlægger en fest.
sentence.en: She must not suspect that we are planning a party.

at anerkende.explanation: "At anerkende" means "to recognize or acknowledge". To say you openly accept that something is true, say: "Jeg anerkender, at jeg tog fejl" (I acknowledge that I was wrong). To know a face again, use "at genkende" (to recognize): "Jeg genkender dig!" (I recognize you!)

sentence.da: Landet vil ikke **anerkende** den nye regering.
sentence.en: The country will not recognize the new government.

at angive.explanation: "At angive" means "to state or indicate". To say you name the reason for something, say: "Hun angav sygdom som årsag" (She gave illness as the reason).

sentence.da: Du skal **angive** din adresse på formularen.
sentence.en: You must state your address on the form.

at angre.explanation: "At angre" means "to regret". To say you regret nothing, say: "Jeg angrer ingenting" (I regret nothing). Do not read "en anger" as the English word "anger": it means "remorse".

sentence.da: Du vil ikke **angre**, at du kom.
sentence.en: You will not regret that you came.

at angribe.explanation: "At angribe" means "to attack". To say a disease harms a body part, use it for the disease: "Sygdommen angriber lungerne" (The disease attacks the lungs).

sentence.da: Hæren vil **angribe** byen ved daggry.
sentence.en: The army will attack the city at dawn.

at angå.explanation: "At angå" means "to concern". To say "as for", use the phrase "hvad angår": "Hvad angår prisen, er den fin" (As for the price, it is fine).

sentence.da: Den nye regel vil **angå** alle i huset.
sentence.en: The new rule will concern everyone in the house.

at anholde.explanation: "At anholde" means "to arrest". To say a person was arrested, use "blive anholdt" (be arrested): "Manden blev anholdt" (The man was arrested).

sentence.da: Politiet kan **anholde** en mand, når han stjæler.
sentence.en: The police can arrest a man when he steals.

at anklage.explanation: "At anklage" means "to charge or accuse". The person who charges someone in court is "en anklager" (a prosecutor).

sentence.da: Han vil **anklage** hende for tyveri.
sentence.en: He will accuse her of theft.

at ankomme.explanation: "At ankomme" means "to arrive". It is built from the verb "at komme" (to come). To say you get to a place, you can also use "at komme frem" (to get there): "Vi kommer frem klokken otte" (We get there at eight).

sentence.da: Flyet skal **ankomme** klokken otte i aften.
sentence.en: The plane is due to arrive at eight tonight.

at anlægge.explanation: "At anlægge" means "to construct or file (a lawsuit)". To say you build something big, such as a road, say: "at anlægge en vej" (to construct a road). To say you start a lawsuit, use "sag" (case) after it: "at anlægge sag mod en virksomhed" (to bring a case against a company).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **anlægge** en ny cykelsti langs vejen.
sentence.en: The municipality will construct a new bike path along the road.

at anmelde.explanation: "At anmelde" means "to report (to police) or review". To say you write about a film or a book for a newspaper, say: "Hun anmelder film for en avis" (She reviews films for a newspaper).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **anmelde** tyveriet til politiet i dag.
sentence.en: I will report the theft to the police today.

at anmode.explanation: "At anmode" means "to request". The thing you send is "en anmodning" (a request).

sentence.da: Han vil **anmode** om orlov i et halvt år.
sentence.en: He wants to request leave for half a year.

at annoncere.explanation: "At annoncere" means "to announce or advertise". To say a band makes news public, say: "Bandet annoncerer en ny turné" (The band announces a new tour).

sentence.da: Butikken vil **annoncere** udsalget i avisen.
sentence.en: The shop will advertise the sale in the newspaper.

at anse.explanation: "At anse" means "to regard or consider". To say how you see yourself, add "for" before the description: "Jeg anser mig selv for heldig" (I consider myself lucky).

sentence.da: Vi må **anse** den gamle bro for farlig.
sentence.en: We must regard the old bridge as dangerous.

at anskaffe.explanation: "At anskaffe" means "to acquire". To say you get a pet, say: "Vi anskaffer en hund" (We are getting a dog). To say you pay money for something, use "at købe" (to buy): "Jeg køber en cykel" (I buy a bike).

sentence.da: Skolen vil **anskaffe** nye computere til eleverne.
sentence.en: The school will acquire new computers for the students.

at anslå.explanation: "At anslå" means "to estimate". To work out an exact figure, use "at beregne" (to calculate): "Jeg beregner prisen" (I calculate the price).

sentence.da: Eksperterne kan **anslå** prisen på huset.
sentence.en: The experts can estimate the price of the house.

at ansætte.explanation: "At ansætte" means "to hire". To say a company takes on new staff, say: "Firmaet ansætter to nye" (The company is hiring two new people).

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **ansætte** en ny kollega.
sentence.en: We would like to hire a new colleague.

at ansøge.explanation: "At ansøge" means "to apply", as in asking formally for a job, a grant or a place. To say you use a rule, use "at anvende" (to use): "Vi anvender reglen" (We apply the rule).

sentence.da: Du kan **ansøge** om en plads på skolen i marts.
sentence.en: You can apply for a place at the school in March.

at antage.explanation: "At antage" means "to assume". It comes from the verb "at tage" (to take).

sentence.da: Vi må **antage**, at toget er forsinket.
sentence.en: We must assume that the train is delayed.

at antyde.explanation: "At antyde" means "to imply". To say you hint at something without saying it, say: "Han antydede, at han var træt" (He hinted that he was tired).

sentence.da: Han ville ikke sige det, men kun **antyde** det.
sentence.en: He did not want to say it, only to imply it.

at anvende.explanation: "At anvende" means "to use or apply". To say a rule forbids using a phone, say: "Man må ikke anvende mobilen under prøven" (You may not use the phone during the test). The plain word for "to use" is "at bruge": "Jeg bruger en blyant" (I use a pencil).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **anvende** en ny metode i timen.
sentence.en: The teacher will use a new method in class.

at appellere.explanation: "At appellere" means "to appeal", as in calling on someone's feelings or sense of duty. To name the feeling, add "til" (to): "Hun appellerer til vores medfølelse" (She appeals to our compassion). To appeal a court ruling, use "at anke" (to appeal a ruling): "Han anker dommen" (He appeals the ruling).

sentence.da: Reklamen skal **appellere** til børn og forældre.
sentence.en: The ad must appeal to children and parents.

at applaudere.explanation: "At applaudere" means "to applaud". To say you approve of an idea or a decision, say: "Jeg applauderer beslutningen" (I applaud the decision).

sentence.da: Publikum vil **applaudere**, når koncerten er slut.
sentence.en: The audience will applaud when the concert is over.

at arbejde.explanation: "At arbejde" means "to work". The noun "et arbejde" means "a job". To say where your job is, say: "Mit arbejde er på et hospital" (My job is at a hospital). It also means work itself: "Jeg har meget arbejde" (I have a lot of work).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **arbejde** på kontoret.
sentence.en: I have to work at the office.

at arbejde hjemmefra.explanation: "At arbejde hjemmefra" means "to work from home". "Hjemmefra" (from home) is built from "hjemme" (at home) and "fra" (from). To say you leave your home, use it for leaving: "Jeg går hjemmefra klokken otte" (I leave home at eight).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **arbejde hjemmefra** på mandag.
sentence.en: I can work from home on Monday.

at arbejde med.explanation: "At arbejde med" means "to work with". To say where you work, use "at arbejde på" (to work at): "Jeg arbejder på kontoret" (I work at the office).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **arbejde med** børn.
sentence.en: I would like to work with children.

at arbejde på.explanation: "At arbejde på" means "to work on". To say where you work, "på" means "at": "Jeg arbejder på kontoret" (I work at the office).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **arbejde på** min rapport i aften.
sentence.en: I want to work on my report tonight.

at argumentere.explanation: "At argumentere" means "to argue", as in giving reasons for a view. To say which view you argue for, add "for" (for): "Hun argumenterer for en kortere arbejdsuge" (She argues for a shorter work week). To quarrel, use "at skændes" (to quarrel): "Børnene skændes om legetøjet" (The children are quarreling about the toy).

sentence.da: Når man skal **argumentere**, må man give gode grunde.
sentence.en: When you argue, you must give good reasons.

at arrangere.explanation: "At arrangere" means "to arrange", as in planning and setting up an event. To put things in order, use "at ordne" (to sort out): "Hun ordner bøgerne" (She is putting the books in order).

sentence.da: Vi vil **arrangere** en fest for hele klassen.
sentence.en: We will arrange a party for the whole class.

at arrestere.explanation: "At arrestere" means "to arrest". To say a person was arrested, say: "Tyven blev arresteret" (The thief was arrested).

sentence.da: Politiet har lov til at **arrestere** en mistænkt.
sentence.en: The police are allowed to arrest a suspect.

at arve.explanation: "At arve" means "to inherit". To say you get a trait from a parent, say: "Hun har arvet sin mors blå øjne" (She has inherited her mother's blue eyes).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **arve** huset, når deres far dør.
sentence.en: The children will inherit the house when their father dies.

atlanterhavet.explanation: "Atlanterhavet" means "the Atlantic Ocean". It ends in "havet" (the ocean), where "-et" already means "the", so you add no separate word for "the".

forms.en: the coast of the Atlantic Ocean

sentence.da: Skibet sejler over **Atlanterhavet** fra Europa til Amerika.
sentence.en: The ship sails across the Atlantic Ocean from Europe to America.

atomkraft.explanation: "Atomkraft" means "nuclear power". It is built from "atom" (atom) and "kraft" (power). To ask whether a country should have it, say: "Skal Danmark have atomkraft?" (Should Denmark have nuclear power?)

sentence.da: Sverige får en del af sin strøm fra **atomkraft**.
sentence.en: Sweden gets part of its electricity from nuclear power.

atten.explanation: "Atten" means "eighteen". In the numbers from "tretten" (thirteen) to "nitten" (nineteen), the ending "-ten" means "ten".

sentence.da: Min søn er **atten** år.
sentence.en: My son is eighteen years old.

atter.explanation: "Atter" means "again". The same meaning is also said with "igen" (again): "Hun er syg igen" (She is ill again).

sentence.da: Efter pausen begyndte musikken **atter** at spille.
sentence.en: After the break the music began to play again.

attraktiv.explanation: "Attraktiv" means "attractive". To describe a person who looks good, say: "en attraktiv mand" (an attractive man).

sentence.da: Byen er **attraktiv** for unge, fordi der er mange uddannelser.
sentence.en: The city is attractive to young people because there are many programs of study.

august.explanation: "August" means "August". Danish writes month names with a lowercase letter, so you write "i august" (in August), not "i August".

sentence.da: Skolen starter igen i **august**.
sentence.en: School starts again in August.

australien.explanation: "Australien" means "Australia". To say you live there, use "i" (in): "Jeg bor i Australien" (I live in Australia). To say you travel there, use "til" (to): "Jeg rejser til Australien" (I am traveling to Australia).

sentence.da: Kænguruer bor i **Australien**.
sentence.en: Kangaroos live in Australia.

autentisk.explanation: "Autentisk" means "authentic". To say a person is true to themselves, say: "Hun er meget autentisk" (She is very true to herself).

sentence.da: Museets stol er **autentisk** og er over to hundrede år gammel.
sentence.en: The museum chair is authentic and is over two hundred years old.

automatisk.explanation: "Automatisk" means "automatic". Do not mix it up with "en automat" (a vending machine). To say you buy a drink from a vending machine, say: "Vi køber en sodavand i en automat" (We buy a soda from a vending machine).

sentence.da: Lyset tændes **automatisk**, når du går ind.
sentence.en: The light comes on automatically when you walk in.

av.explanation: "Av" means "ouch". To say something hurts, say: "Av, min fod!" (Ouch, my foot!) To react to a small slip, say "ups" (oops): "Ups, jeg tabte koppen!" (Oops, I dropped the cup!)

sentence.da: **Av**, den kop er varm!
sentence.en: Ouch, that cup is hot!

avanceret.explanation: "Avanceret" means "advanced". To say a program is too difficult for you, say: "Programmet er for avanceret for mig" (The program is too advanced for me).

sentence.da: Den nye telefon er meget **avanceret**, men let at bruge.
sentence.en: The new phone is very advanced, but easy to use.

en a-kasse.explanation: "En a-kasse" means "an unemployment insurance fund", an organization that Danes pay a monthly fee to, as protection for the time between jobs. The "A" stands for "arbejdsløshed" (unemployment).

sentence.da: Når jeg mister mit job, får jeg penge fra min **a-kasse**.
sentence.en: When I lose my job, I get money from my unemployment fund.

en abe.explanation: "En abe" means "a monkey or ape". Danish uses one word for both. To talk about a great ape, use "en menneskeabe" (literally, a human ape): "En gorilla er en menneskeabe" (A gorilla is a great ape).

sentence.da: En **abe** klatrer op i det høje træ.
sentence.en: A monkey climbs up the tall tree.

en aborre.explanation: "En aborre" means "a perch", as in the fish. To say you catch this fish, say: "at fange en aborre" (to catch a perch). It is a common freshwater fish in Danish lakes.

sentence.da: Fisken med de mørke striber i søen er en **aborre**.
sentence.en: The fish with the dark stripes in the lake is a perch.

en abort.explanation: "En abort" means "an abortion or miscarriage". To say which one, add a word: "en provokeret abort" (an induced abortion) and "en spontan abort" (a miscarriage).

sentence.da: En **abort** afslutter et svangerskab, før barnet bliver født.
sentence.en: An abortion ends a pregnancy before the baby is born.

en abrikos.explanation: "En abrikos" means "an apricot". To talk about the dried fruit, say: "tørrede abrikoser" (dried apricots).

sentence.da: En **abrikos** er lille og orange.
sentence.en: An apricot is small and orange.

en accent.explanation: "En accent" means "an accent", as in the way someone speaks. It also means the small mark over a letter, like the é in "café". To say the mark is there, say: "Café har en accent over e'et" (Café has an accent over the e).

sentence.da: Hun taler dansk med en tydelig **accent**.
sentence.en: She speaks Danish with a clear accent.

en adgangskode.explanation: "En adgangskode" means "a password". It is built from "adgang" (access) and "kode" (code). The word "adgang" is also on the sign "Ingen adgang" (No entry).

sentence.da: Jeg har glemt min **adgangskode**.
sentence.en: I forgot my password.

en admiral.explanation: "En admiral" means "an admiral". Do not mix it up with "en general" (a general), which is a rank in the army: "Generalen leder hæren" (The general leads the army).

sentence.da: En **admiral** leder mange skibe på havet.
sentence.en: An admiral leads many ships at sea.

en adoption.explanation: "En adoption" means "an adoption". To say a child is given up for adoption, use "at give et barn til adoption" (to give a child up for adoption).

sentence.da: Ved **adoption** bliver barnet en del af en ny familie.
sentence.en: With adoption, the child becomes part of a new family.

en adresse.explanation: "En adresse" means "an address". To ask for someone's address, say: "Hvad er din adresse?" (What is your address?)

sentence.da: Jeg skriver min **adresse** på brevet: Vestergade 12.
sentence.en: I write my address on the letter: Vestergade 12.

en advarsel.explanation: "En advarsel" means "a warning". To say someone warns you, say: "Han gav mig en advarsel" (He gave me a warning).

sentence.da: Der er en **advarsel** om kraftig regn i dag.
sentence.en: There is a warning about heavy rain today.

en adventskrans.explanation: "En adventskrans" means "an Advent wreath". It is built from "advent" (Advent) and "en krans" (a wreath). In Denmark, it is set out in the weeks before December 24.

sentence.da: En **adventskrans** har fire lys, og vi tænder ét hver søndag.
sentence.en: An Advent wreath has four candles, and we light one each Sunday.

en advokat.explanation: "En advokat" means "a lawyer". To say you hire one, say: "at hyre en advokat" (to hire a lawyer).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til en **advokat**, fordi jeg har en retssag.
sentence.en: I am calling a lawyer because I have a court case.

en afbetaling.explanation: "En afbetaling" means "an installment plan". It is built from "af" (off) and "en betaling" (a payment).

sentence.da: Sofaen kan købes på **afbetaling** over tolv måneder.
sentence.en: The sofa can be bought on installments over twelve months.

en afbrydelse.explanation: "En afbrydelse" means "an interruption". To say the power stops for a while, say: "en afbrydelse i strømmen" (an interruption in the power). Do not mix it up with "en pause" (a break): "en pause på ti minutter" (a ten-minute break).

sentence.da: Vi kan arbejde i to timer uden **afbrydelse**.
sentence.en: We can work for two hours without interruption.

en afdeling.explanation: "En afdeling" means "a department". To name a department by its job, put the job in front: "en salgsafdeling" (a sales department).

sentence.da: Banken har en **afdeling** for lån.
sentence.en: The bank has a department for loans.

en afdelingsleder.explanation: "En afdelingsleder" means "a department manager". It is built from "afdeling" (department) and "leder" (leader).

sentence.da: En **afdelingsleder** har ansvaret for alle i sin afdeling.
sentence.en: A department manager is responsible for everyone in their department.

en affaldssortering.explanation: "En affaldssortering" means "a waste sorting". It is built from "affald" (waste) and "en sortering" (a sorting).

sentence.da: Ved **affaldssortering** kommer glas, papir og plast i hver sin spand.
sentence.en: With waste sorting, glass, paper and plastic go in separate bins.

en affære.explanation: "En affære" means "an affair", as in a secret love relationship. It also means a matter or business. To say something is a costly business, say: "en dyr affære" (an expensive business).

sentence.da: Han havde en hemmelig **affære** med en kollega.
sentence.en: He had a secret affair with a colleague.

en afgang.explanation: "En afgang" means "a departure". To ask when the next train leaves, say: "Hvornår er næste afgang?" (When is the next departure?)

sentence.da: Næste **afgang** er klokken ni.
sentence.en: The next departure is at nine.

en afgangseksamen.explanation: "En afgangseksamen" means "a final exam". It is built from "afgang" (departure) and "en eksamen" (an exam), so it is the exam you take when you leave the school.

sentence.da: Efter **afgangseksamen** får eleverne deres eksamensbevis.
sentence.en: After the final exam, the students get their diploma.

en afgift.explanation: "En afgift" means "a levy". To say the state charges money on a thing, say: "en afgift på plastikposer" (a levy on plastic bags). A charge on what you earn is "en skat" (a tax): "Jeg betaler skat" (I pay tax).

sentence.da: Der er en høj **afgift** på cigaretter og alkohol i Danmark.
sentence.en: There is a high levy on cigarettes and alcohol in Denmark.

en afgrøde.explanation: "En afgrøde" means "a crop". To say the year's crop turned out well, say: "en god afgrøde" (a good crop).

sentence.da: Raps er en gul **afgrøde**, og man laver olie af den.
sentence.en: Rapeseed is a yellow crop, and oil is made from it.

en afgørelse.explanation: "En afgørelse" means "a decision or ruling". To say an authority's decision cannot be changed, say: "Nævnets afgørelse er endelig" (The board's ruling is final). To talk about a decision you make yourself, use "en beslutning" (a decision): "Jeg har taget en beslutning" (I have made a decision).

sentence.da: Kommunen sendte sin **afgørelse** med posten, og vi kan klage over den.
sentence.en: The municipality sent its decision by mail, and we can appeal it.

en afhandling.explanation: "En afhandling" means "a thesis". To say a thesis written for a doctorate, use "en ph.d.-afhandling" (a PhD thesis).

sentence.da: Når man skriver en lang **afhandling**, studerer man ét emne i dybden.
sentence.en: When you write a long thesis, you study one subject in depth.

en afhentning.explanation: "En afhentning" means "a pickup". To say what is collected, add "af" (of): "afhentning af pakker" (pickup of parcels).

sentence.da: Du kan vælge **afhentning** i butikken i stedet for levering.
sentence.en: You can choose pickup in the store instead of delivery.

en afhængighed.explanation: "En afhængighed" means "an addiction or dependence". When you talk about needing other people, it means "dependence": "afhængighed af hinanden" (dependence on each other).

sentence.da: Hans **afhængighed** af spil kostede ham alle hans penge.
sentence.en: His addiction to gambling cost him all his money.

en afhøring.explanation: "En afhøring" means "an interrogation". It comes from the verb "at afhøre" (to question).

sentence.da: Ved en **afhøring** spørger politiet om, hvad der skete.
sentence.en: At an interrogation, the police ask what happened.

en afklaring.explanation: "En afklaring" means "a clarification". To talk about getting the price settled, say: "en afklaring af prisen" (a clarification of the price). Do not mix it up with "en forklaring" (an explanation): "Jeg vil have en forklaring" (I want an explanation).

sentence.da: Vi venter på en **afklaring**, før vi kan beslutte noget.
sentence.en: We are waiting for a clarification before we can decide anything.

en afkørsel.explanation: "En afkørsel" means "an exit", as in leaving a big road. To leave a building, use "en udgang" (an exit): "Udgangen er til højre" (The exit is on the right).

sentence.da: Tag næste **afkørsel** og drej til højre.
sentence.en: Take the next exit and turn right.

en aflevering.explanation: "En aflevering" means "a submission". To talk about giving something back, add "af" (of): "aflevering af nøgler" (returning the keys).

sentence.da: Jeg skal skrive min **aflevering** færdig i aften.
sentence.en: I have to finish writing my submission tonight.

en afleveringsfrist.explanation: "En afleveringsfrist" means "a submission deadline". It is built from "at aflevere" (to hand in) and "en frist" (a time limit).

sentence.da: Vi har en **afleveringsfrist** på fredag klokken tolv.
sentence.en: We have a submission deadline on Friday at twelve o'clock.

en aflysning.explanation: "En aflysning" means "a cancellation". It comes from the verb "at aflyse" (to cancel).

sentence.da: Der kom en **aflysning** af flyet på grund af stormen.
sentence.en: There was a cancellation of the flight because of the storm.

en afløser.explanation: "En afløser" means "a substitute". Do not mix it up with "en afløsning" (a relief). "En afløser" is the person: "Afløseren kommer klokken otte" (The substitute comes at eight o'clock). "En afløsning" is the act of taking over: "Natholdet får afløsning klokken seks" (The night team gets relief at six o'clock).

sentence.da: Læreren er syg, og en **afløser** underviser klassen i dag.
sentence.en: The teacher is sick, and a substitute is teaching the class today.

en afløsning.explanation: "En afløsning" means "a relief or replacement". When a caregiver at home gets help so they can take a break, Danish uses this word too: "Hun får afløsning to timer om ugen" (She gets relief two hours a week). Do not mix it up with "en afløser" (a substitute). "En afløsning" is the act of taking over, and "en afløser" is the person: "Afløseren kommer klokken otte" (The substitute comes at eight o'clock).

sentence.da: Når morgenholdet kommer, får natholdet **afløsning**.
sentence.en: When the morning team arrives, the night team gets relief.

en afrejse.explanation: "En afrejse" means "a departure". It is built from "af" (off) and the verb "at rejse" (to travel). Do not mix it up with "en afgang" (a departure). "En afgang" is when a train or bus leaves a stop: "Afgang fra spor 3 er klokken ti" (Departure from platform 3 is at ten o'clock).

sentence.da: Vores **afrejse** er tidligt på fredag.
sentence.en: Our departure is early on Friday.

en afrikaner.explanation: "En afrikaner" means "an African". It is built from "Afrika" (Africa). Danish writes it with a small first letter: "afrikaner", not "Afrikaner".

sentence.da: Min nabo er **afrikaner** og kommer fra Kenya.
sentence.en: My neighbor is African and comes from Kenya.

en afsked.explanation: "En afsked" means "a farewell". To say you say goodbye to someone, use "at tage" (to take) and "med" (with): "Jeg tager afsked med min ven" (I say goodbye to my friend).

sentence.da: Vi tog **afsked** på stationen.
sentence.en: We said goodbye at the station.

en afslutning.explanation: "En afslutning" means "an ending". It comes from the verb "at afslutte" (to finish). In a Danish school, "afslutning" is also the party at the end of the school year: "Vi har afslutning i skolen i morgen" (We have the end-of-year party at school tomorrow).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide filmens **afslutning**.
sentence.en: I like the ending of the film.

en afstand.explanation: "En afstand" means "a distance". To ask how far away a place is, say "afstanden til" (the distance to): "Hvad er afstanden til stationen?" (What is the distance to the station?) To tell someone to stay back, say "Hold afstand!" (Keep your distance!)

sentence.da: Der er en **afstand** på to kilometer til byen.
sentence.en: There is a distance of two kilometers to the town.

en afstemning.explanation: "En afstemning" means "a vote". Do not mix it up with "et valg" (an election). "En afstemning" is a vote on a question: "Der er afstemning om forslaget" (There is a vote on the proposal). "Et valg" is when people choose a person: "Klubben har valg til bestyrelsen" (The club has an election for the board).

sentence.da: Ved en **afstemning** tæller man stemmerne, og flertallet vinder.
sentence.en: In a vote, you count the votes, and the majority wins.

en aftale.explanation: "En aftale" means "an appointment or agreement". When you book a time with someone and want to move it, say "Kan vi flytte aftalen til fredag?" (Can we move the appointment to Friday?) When two people agree on something, you can say "Det er en aftale!" (It's a deal!)

sentence.da: Jeg har en **aftale** med lægen.
sentence.en: I have an appointment with the doctor.

en aften.explanation: "En aften" means "an evening". To say "tonight", use "i aften": "Vi ses i aften" (See you tonight).

sentence.da: Vi spiser mad hver **aften**.
sentence.en: We eat food every evening.

en aftenrutine.explanation: "En aftenrutine" means "an evening routine". It is built from "aften" (evening) and "rutine" (routine). The part "aften" is also in "aftensmad" (dinner): "Hvad skal vi have til aftensmad?" (What are we having for dinner?)

sentence.da: Min **aftenrutine** er te, en bog og tidlig seng.
sentence.en: My evening routine is tea, a book and an early bed.

en aftenskole.explanation: "En aftenskole" means "an evening class". In Denmark, adults can take courses in the evening at a school of this kind, in subjects such as languages, cooking or painting. It is built from "aften" (evening) and "skole" (school).

sentence.da: Min mor går på **aftenskole** for at lære spansk.
sentence.en: My mother goes to evening classes to learn Spanish.

en aftentur.explanation: "En aftentur" means "an evening walk". It is built from "aften" (evening) and "tur" (walk, trip). To suggest a walk without saying when, use "tur" with "at tage" (to take): "Skal vi tage en tur?" (Shall we go for a walk?)

sentence.da: Efter maden tager vi en **aftentur** langs vandet.
sentence.en: After dinner we take an evening walk along the water.

en aftrækker.explanation: "En aftrækker" means "a trigger", as in the part of a gun. Do not use it for something that sets off a reaction. That is "en udløser" (a trigger): "Stress kan være en udløser for migræne" (Stress can be a trigger for migraine).

sentence.da: Pistolen har en **aftrækker**, som man trykker på for at skyde.
sentence.en: The pistol has a trigger that you press to shoot.

en afveksling.explanation: "En afveksling" means "a variety or change". To say someone does something for a change, use "til afveksling": "Til afveksling lavede han mad" (For a change, he cooked).

sentence.da: Efter mange dage inde var en tur i skoven en dejlig **afveksling**.
sentence.en: After many days indoors, a walk in the forest was a lovely change.

en afvigelse.explanation: "En afvigelse" means "a deviation". It comes from the verb "at afvige" (to deviate).

sentence.da: Termometeret viser en **afvigelse** på to grader fra normalen.
sentence.en: The thermometer shows a deviation of two degrees from normal.

en agent.explanation: "En agent" means "an agent", as in a person who handles deals for an actor or athlete. When you talk about a spy, it has a different meaning: "en hemmelig agent" (a secret agent).

sentence.da: En **agent** forhandler kontrakter for en skuespiller eller atlet.
sentence.en: An agent negotiates contracts for an actor or athlete.

en agurk.explanation: "En agurk" means "a cucumber". To talk about cucumbers kept in a jar, use "syltede agurker" (pickled cucumbers): "Der er syltede agurker i glasset" (There are pickled cucumbers in the jar).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer en **agurk** til salaten.
sentence.en: I am cutting a cucumber for the salad.

en airbag.explanation: "En airbag" means "an airbag". When you write "the airbag", double the g: "airbaggen", not "airbagen".

sentence.da: Min nye bil har en **airbag** i rattet.
sentence.en: My new car has an airbag in the steering wheel.

en airfryer.explanation: "En airfryer" means "an air fryer". Danish writes it as one word, "airfryer", not as two words like English.

sentence.da: Man kan lave pommes frites i en **airfryer**.
sentence.en: You can make fries in an air fryer.

en aktie.explanation: "En aktie" means "a share", as in a part of a company. To say which company, add "i" (in): "Hun ejer aktier i et dansk firma" (She owns shares in a Danish company).

sentence.da: Når man køber en **aktie**, ejer man en lille del af firmaet.
sentence.en: When you buy a share, you own a small part of the company.

en aktiekurs.explanation: "En aktiekurs" means "a share price". It is built from "aktie" (share) and "kurs" (rate). To say the price goes down, use "at falde" (to fall): "Aktiekursen faldt i dag" (The share price fell today).

sentence.da: Hvis mange vil købe en aktie, stiger dens **aktiekurs**.
sentence.en: If many people want to buy a share, its share price rises.

en aktivitet.explanation: "En aktivitet" means "an activity". When a school or club plans things for a group to do, Danish uses the plural: "Der er mange aktiviteter for børn i sommerferien" (There are many activities for children in the summer holiday).

sentence.da: Svømning er en sjov **aktivitet** for hele familien.
sentence.en: Swimming is a fun activity for the whole family.

en akvariefisk.explanation: "En akvariefisk" means "an aquarium fish". It is built from "akvarium" (aquarium) and "fisk" (fish). For more than one fish, the word stays the same, with no ending: "Vi har fem akvariefisk" (We have five aquarium fish).

sentence.da: En **akvariefisk** lever i et akvarium med planter.
sentence.en: An aquarium fish lives in an aquarium with plants.

en alarm.explanation: "En alarm" means "an alarm". When a warning sounds, say "Alarmen går!" (The alarm is going off!) To set a wake-up alarm on your phone, say "Jeg stiller en alarm til klokken syv" (I set an alarm for seven o'clock).

sentence.da: Min **alarm** ringer klokken seks hver morgen.
sentence.en: My alarm rings at six every morning.

en alarmklokke.explanation: "En alarmklokke" means "an alarm bell". It is built from "alarm" (alarm) and "klokke" (bell). The part "klokke" also means "clock" when you ask the time: "Hvad er klokken?" (What time is it?)

sentence.da: Vi hørte en **alarmklokke** ringe midt om natten.
sentence.en: We heard an alarm bell ring in the middle of the night.

en albue.explanation: "En albue" means "an elbow". Danish can use "albuen" (the elbow) for your own elbow: "Jeg har slået albuen" (I hit my elbow), literally "I hit the elbow".

sentence.da: Armen bøjer ved din **albue**.
sentence.en: The arm bends at your elbow.

en alder.explanation: "En alder" means "an age". To ask how old someone is, Danish does not use "alder". It uses "gammel" (old): "Hvor gammel er du?" (How old are you?) To say "at my age", use "i min alder": "Det er svært i min alder" (It is hard at my age).

sentence.da: På blanketten skal du skrive din **alder**.
sentence.en: On the form, you have to write your age.

en algoritme.explanation: "En algoritme" means "an algorithm". Danish spells it without an "h": "algoritme", not "algorithm".

sentence.da: En **algoritme** er en række trin, som computeren følger.
sentence.en: An algorithm is a series of steps that the computer follows.

en alkoholiker.explanation: "En alkoholiker" means "an alcoholic". It is built from "alkohol" (alcohol). Danish spells it with "k", not "c".

sentence.da: Som **alkoholiker** kan han ikke drikke bare ét glas.
sentence.en: As an alcoholic he cannot drink even one glass.

en allergi.explanation: "En allergi" means "an allergy". To name what you react to, put its name in front of "allergi" as one word: "en pollenallergi" (a pollen allergy).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **allergi** mod nødder.
sentence.en: I have an allergy to nuts.

en alliance.explanation: "En alliance" means "an alliance". To say who the alliance is with, add "med" (with): "Vi har en alliance med vores naboer" (We have an alliance with our neighbors).

sentence.da: Landene dannede en **alliance** for at beskytte hinanden.
sentence.en: The countries formed an alliance to protect each other.

en allieret.explanation: "En allieret" means "an ally". When you talk about history, "de allierede" (the allies) are the countries that fought Germany in World War II: "Danmark blev befriet af de allierede i 1945" (Denmark was freed by the Allies in 1945).

sentence.da: Hvis et land er din **allieret**, hjælper det dig i krig.
sentence.en: If a country is your ally, it helps you in war.

en altan.explanation: "En altan" means "a balcony". The part "altan" is also in "en altankasse" (a balcony planter box): "Jeg har blomster i en altankasse" (I have flowers in a balcony planter box).
