sentence.da: Vi sidder på vores **altan** og nyder solen.
sentence.en: We sit on our balcony and enjoy the sun.

en amatør.explanation: "En amatør" means "an amateur". To call a person who does a poor job an amateur, say "Sikke en amatør!" (What an amateur!) This is an insult.

sentence.da: Han er **amatør** og spiller fodbold uden at få penge.
sentence.en: He is an amateur and plays soccer without getting paid.

en ambassade.explanation: "En ambassade" means "an embassy". To say you are going to the embassy, use "på" (at): "Vi skal på ambassaden i morgen" (We are going to the embassy tomorrow).

sentence.da: Vi fik hjælp fra den danske **ambassade** i Rom.
sentence.en: We got help from the Danish embassy in Rome.

en ambassadør.explanation: "En ambassadør" means "an ambassador". When a well-known person speaks for a cause, the word fits too: "Hun er ambassadør for en velgørenhedsorganisation" (She is an ambassador for a charity).

sentence.da: Hver **ambassadør** repræsenterer sit land i udlandet.
sentence.en: Each ambassador represents their country abroad.

en ambition.explanation: "En ambition" means "an ambition". To say someone has big goals, use "at have" (to have) and the plural: "De har store ambitioner for firmaet" (They have big ambitions for the firm).

sentence.da: Hun har en stor **ambition** om at blive læge.
sentence.en: She has a big ambition to become a doctor.

en ambulance.explanation: "En ambulance" means "an ambulance". In Denmark, you call the emergency number 112 to get one: "Ring til 112!" (Call 112!)

sentence.da: Han er meget syg. Ring efter en **ambulance**!
sentence.en: He is very sick. Call for an ambulance!

en amerikaner.explanation: "En amerikaner" means "an American". It is built from "Amerika" (America). Danish writes it with a small first letter: "amerikaner", not "Amerikaner". In a Danish bakery, "en amerikaner" is also a flat, round cake with icing: "Vi køber to amerikanere hos bageren" (We buy two amerikaner cakes at the baker).

sentence.da: Hun er **amerikaner** og bor i Danmark.
sentence.en: She is American and lives in Denmark.

en analyse.explanation: "En analyse" means "an analysis". To say what you analyze, add "af" (of): "Vi laver en analyse af tallene" (We do an analysis of the numbers).

sentence.da: Efter en grundig **analyse** kender vi årsagen til problemet.
sentence.en: After a thorough analysis we know the cause of the problem.

en ananas.explanation: "En ananas" means "a pineapple". Danish doubles the s before an ending, so "the pineapple" is "ananassen" with two s's.

sentence.da: En **ananas** er sød og gul indeni.
sentence.en: A pineapple is sweet and yellow inside.

en anbefaling.explanation: "En anbefaling" means "a recommendation". To say who told you about a place, use "på anbefaling af" (on the recommendation of): "Vi kom på anbefaling af en ven" (We came on a friend's recommendation).

sentence.da: Tak for din **anbefaling** af restauranten.
sentence.en: Thanks for your recommendation of the restaurant.

en and.explanation: "En and" means "a duck". The form for "the duck" is "anden". The same spelling is also the word for "the other". To talk about the duck, say "Anden svømmer" (The duck swims). To point to the other one of two things, say "Jeg tager den anden" (I take the other one).

sentence.da: En **and** svømmer på søen.
sentence.en: A duck is swimming on the lake.

en andel.explanation: "En andel" means "a share or portion". To talk about a part of a whole group, use "andelen af" (the share of): "Andelen af ældre vokser" (The share of older people is growing). The word "andel" is also in "en andelsbolig" (a cooperative apartment): "Vi bor i en andelsbolig" (We live in a cooperative apartment).

sentence.da: Hver af os betaler en lige stor **andel** af regningen.
sentence.en: Each of us pays an equal share of the bill.

en andelsbolig.explanation: "En andelsbolig" means "a cooperative apartment". It is built from "andel" (share) and "bolig" (home). In Denmark, the monthly fee you pay for one is called "boligafgift" (housing fee).

sentence.da: I en **andelsbolig** ejer du en andel af foreningen, ikke selve lejligheden.
sentence.en: In a cooperative apartment you own a share of the association, not the apartment itself.

en anekdote.explanation: "En anekdote" means "an anecdote". Danish spells it with "k", not "c": "anekdote".

sentence.da: Han fortalte en sjov **anekdote** om sin første dag på arbejde.
sentence.en: He told a funny anecdote about his first day at work.

en anelse.explanation: "En anelse" means "a hint or slight idea". To say something is a touch better, put "en anelse" before the describing word: "Det er en anelse bedre" (It is a touch better). To ask whether someone has any idea, say "Har du en anelse om hvorfor?" (Do you have any idea why?)

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke den mindste **anelse** om, hvor nøglerne er.
sentence.en: I do not have the slightest idea where the keys are.

en anfører.explanation: "En anfører" means "a captain (team)". It comes from the verb "at anføre" (to lead).

sentence.da: Hun er holdets **anfører** og leder spillerne på banen.
sentence.en: She is the team's captain and leads the players on the field.

en angriber.explanation: "En angriber" means "a forward or attacker". Outside sport, when someone attacks a person, use it for "attacker": "Angriberen løb væk" (The attacker ran away).

sentence.da: En **angriber** skal score mål, mens forsvaret skal stoppe modstanderen.
sentence.en: A forward must score goals, while the defense must stop the opponent.

en anholdelse.explanation: "En anholdelse" means "an arrest". To say a person was arrested, use "anholdt" (arrested) with "blive" (to be): "Han blev anholdt i går" (He was arrested yesterday).

sentence.da: Efter indbruddet foretog politiet en **anholdelse**.
sentence.en: After the burglary, the police made an arrest.

en ankel.explanation: "En ankel" means "an ankle". To say you sprained your ankle, use "at forstuve" (to sprain): "Jeg har forstuvet anklen" (I have sprained my ankle).

sentence.da: Din **ankel** sidder mellem foden og underbenet.
sentence.en: Your ankle is between the foot and the lower leg.

en anklage.explanation: "En anklage" means "an accusation". It comes from the verb "at anklage" (to accuse). To say someone brings an accusation, use "at rejse" (to raise): "De rejser en anklage mod ham" (They bring an accusation against him).

sentence.da: Der er en alvorlig **anklage** mod ham.
sentence.en: There is a serious accusation against him.

en anklager.explanation: "En anklager" means "a prosecutor". Do not mix it up with "en anklage" (an accusation). "En anklager" is a person: "Anklageren taler i retten" (The prosecutor speaks in court). "En anklage" is a statement against someone: "Anklagen er alvorlig" (The accusation is serious).

sentence.da: En **anklager** forsøger at bevise, at den tiltalte er skyldig.
sentence.en: A prosecutor tries to prove that the defendant is guilty.

en ankomst.explanation: "En ankomst" means "an arrival". To say "on arrival", use "ved ankomsten": "Ved ankomsten skal du vise dit pas" (On arrival you must show your passport).

sentence.da: Vores **ankomst** er klokken tolv.
sentence.en: Our arrival is at twelve.

en ankomsthal.explanation: "En ankomsthal" means "an arrivals hall". It is built from "ankomst" (arrival) and "hal" (hall). The part "hal" is also in "en idrætshal" (a sports hall): "Vi spiller håndbold i idrætshallen" (We play handball in the sports hall).

sentence.da: Passagererne kommer ud i en **ankomsthal** efter landingen.
sentence.en: The passengers come out into an arrivals hall after landing.

en anledning.explanation: "En anledning" means "an occasion". When you talk about a reason to do something, the word means "reason": "Jeg har ingen anledning til at klage" (I have no reason to complain).

sentence.da: Vi holder en fest i **anledning** af hendes fødselsdag.
sentence.en: We are having a party on the occasion of her birthday.

en anmeldelse.explanation: "En anmeldelse" means "a review", as in a written opinion of a book, film or restaurant. When you report a crime to the police, the word is "en politianmeldelse": "Jeg vil gerne lave en politianmeldelse" (I would like to file a police report).

sentence.da: Jeg læste en **anmeldelse** af filmen, før jeg købte billetter.
sentence.en: I read a review of the movie before I bought tickets.

en anmelder.explanation: "En anmelder" means "a reviewer or critic". When someone reports a crime to the police, that person is "anmelderen": "Anmelderen ringede til politiet" (The person who reported the crime called the police).

sentence.da: Som **anmelder** ser hun mange film og skriver om dem i avisen.
sentence.en: As a reviewer, she sees many films and writes about them in the paper.

en anmodning.explanation: "En anmodning" means "a request". It is a formal word. For an everyday request, use "at bede om" (to ask for): "Jeg vil bede om hjælp" (I would like to ask for help).

sentence.da: Myndighederne har modtaget din **anmodning** og svarer inden for en uge.
sentence.en: The authorities have received your request and will answer within a week.

en annonce.explanation: "En annonce" means "an advertisement". For an ad on TV, use "en reklame" (a commercial): "Der er en reklame i fjernsynet" (There is a commercial on TV).

sentence.da: Jeg så en **annonce** for en ny telefon.
sentence.en: I saw an ad for a new phone.

en ansat.explanation: "En ansat" means "an employee". To say you work for a company, use "er ansat" (am employed): "Jeg er ansat her" (I am employed here).

sentence.da: Hver **ansat** får en ny telefon.
sentence.en: Every employee gets a new phone.

en ansigtscreme.explanation: "En ansigtscreme" means "a face cream". Danish spells "cream" as "creme", and joins "ansigt" (face) to it with an "s".

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **ansigtscreme** hver morgen, fordi min hud er tør.
sentence.en: I use face cream every morning because my skin is dry.

en ansættelse.explanation: "En ansættelse" means "an employment or hiring". To say who is being hired, add "af" (of): "ansættelsen af en ny chef" (the hiring of a new boss).

sentence.da: Ved **ansættelse** skriver man under på en kontrakt.
sentence.en: When someone is hired, they sign a contract.

en ansættelseskontrakt.explanation: "En ansættelseskontrakt" means "an employment contract". It is built from "ansættelse" (employment) and "kontrakt" (contract). To say you signed it, use "at skrive under på" (to sign): "Jeg skrev under på ansættelseskontrakten i går" (I signed the employment contract yesterday).

sentence.da: I din **ansættelseskontrakt** står der, hvor meget du får i løn.
sentence.en: Your employment contract says how much pay you get.

en ansættelsessamtale.explanation: "En ansættelsessamtale" means "a job interview". It is built from "ansættelse" (employment) and "samtale" (conversation). Another word for the same thing is "en jobsamtale": "Jeg har en jobsamtale i morgen" (I have a job interview tomorrow).

sentence.da: Til en **ansættelsessamtale** fortæller du, hvorfor du passer til jobbet.
sentence.en: At a job interview you explain why you fit the job.

en ansøgning.explanation: "En ansøgning" means "an application". To say what you apply for, add "om" (for): "Hun skriver en ansøgning om et job" (She writes an application for a job).

sentence.da: Jeg har sendt min **ansøgning** til firmaet.
sentence.en: I have sent my application to the company.

en ansøgningsfrist.explanation: "En ansøgningsfrist" means "an application deadline". It is built from "ansøgning" (application) and "frist" (deadline). To say you meet it, use "at overholde" (to keep to): "Du skal overholde ansøgningsfristen" (You must meet the application deadline).

sentence.da: Den næste **ansøgningsfrist** til uddannelsen er den første marts.
sentence.en: The next application deadline for the program is March first.

en antagelse.explanation: "En antagelse" means "an assumption". It comes from the verb "at antage" (to assume). To say an assumption is fair, use "rimelig" (reasonable): "Det er en rimelig antagelse" (That is a fair assumption).

sentence.da: Det var kun en **antagelse**, ikke et bevis.
sentence.en: It was only an assumption, not proof.

en antydning.explanation: "En antydning" means "a hint". To say someone hinted at something, use "give en antydning af" (give a hint of): "Hun gav en antydning af, at hun ville flytte" (She dropped a hint that she would move). Do not mix it up with "en anelse" (a slight idea). "En anelse" is what you have yourself: "Jeg har en anelse om svaret" (I have a slight idea of the answer).

sentence.da: Der var en **antydning** af et smil i hans ansigt.
sentence.en: There was a hint of a smile on his face.

en apoteker.explanation: "En apoteker" means "a pharmacist". It is built from "apotek" (pharmacy). To say you are going to the pharmacy, use "på apoteket": "Jeg skal på apoteket" (I am going to the pharmacy).

sentence.da: Du kan spørge en **apoteker** om, hvordan medicinen virker.
sentence.en: You can ask a pharmacist how the medicine works.

en app.explanation: "En app" means "an app". To tell someone to open one, use "at åbne" (to open): "Åbn appen" (Open the app).

sentence.da: Jeg henter en **app** til min telefon.
sentence.en: I am downloading an app for my phone.

en appelsin.explanation: "En appelsin" means "an orange", as in the fruit. For the color, Danish uses "orange": "en orange bold" (an orange ball).

sentence.da: Af en **appelsin** kan man presse juice.
sentence.en: You can squeeze juice from an orange.

en araber.explanation: "En araber" means "an Arab". Danish writes it with a small first letter: "araber", not "Araber". To name the language, use "arabisk" (Arabic): "Han taler arabisk" (He speaks Arabic).

sentence.da: Min nabo er **araber** og taler både arabisk og dansk.
sentence.en: My neighbor is an Arab and speaks both Arabic and Danish.

en arbejdsbyrde.explanation: "En arbejdsbyrde" means "a workload". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "byrde" (burden). To say the work is too much, call the workload heavy: "en tung arbejdsbyrde" (a heavy workload).

sentence.da: Min **arbejdsbyrde** er for stor, fordi vi mangler to kolleger.
sentence.en: My workload is too big because we are missing two colleagues.

en arbejdsdag.explanation: "En arbejdsdag" means "a working day". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "dag" (day). To say a day at work is long, say "en lang arbejdsdag" (a long working day).

sentence.da: Min **arbejdsdag** slutter klokken fire.
sentence.en: My working day ends at four o'clock.

en arbejdsgiver.explanation: "En arbejdsgiver" means "an employer". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "at give" (to give). The ending "giver" is also in "en rådgiver" (an adviser), someone who gives råd (advice): "Hun er min rådgiver" (She is my adviser).

sentence.da: Min **arbejdsgiver** betaler for kurset.
sentence.en: My employer pays for the course.

en arbejdsopgave.explanation: "En arbejdsopgave" means "a work task". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "opgave" (task). To say you have been given a new one, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg har fået en ny arbejdsopgave" (I have a new work task).

sentence.da: Min vigtigste **arbejdsopgave** er at svare på kundernes spørgsmål.
sentence.en: My most important work task is to answer customers' questions.

en arbejdsplads.explanation: "En arbejdsplads" means "a workplace". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "plads" (place). The part "plads" also means room or space: "Der er plads til alle" (There is room for everyone).

sentence.da: Jeg ser mine kolleger på min **arbejdsplads**.
sentence.en: I see my colleagues at my workplace.

en arbejdsskade.explanation: "En arbejdsskade" means "a work injury". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "skade" (injury). In Denmark, a work injury can give you the right to compensation.

sentence.da: Man kan få en **arbejdsskade** i ryggen, når man løfter på den forkerte måde.
sentence.en: You can get a work injury in the back when you lift the wrong way.

en arbejdstager.explanation: "En arbejdstager" means "an employee". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "at tage" (to take): the one who takes work. The opposite is "en arbejdsgiver" (an employer): "Arbejdsgiveren betaler arbejdstageren" (The employer pays the employee).

sentence.da: Som **arbejdstager** har du ret til betalt ferie.
sentence.en: As an employee you have a right to paid vacation.

en arbejdstilladelse.explanation: "En arbejdstilladelse" means "a work permit". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "tilladelse" (permission). To say you are applying for one, use "at søge om" (to apply for): "Jeg søger om en arbejdstilladelse" (I am applying for a work permit).

sentence.da: Mange udlændinge skal have en **arbejdstilladelse** for at arbejde i Danmark.
sentence.en: Many foreigners must have a work permit to work in Denmark.

en arkitekt.explanation: "En arkitekt" means "an architect". Danish spells it with "k", not "ch": "arkitekt".

sentence.da: Min søster er **arkitekt** og tegner huse.
sentence.en: My sister is an architect and draws houses.

en arm.explanation: "En arm" means "an arm". Danish can use "armen" (the arm) for your own arm: "Hun har brækket armen" (She has broken her arm), literally "She has broken the arm".

sentence.da: Hånden sidder for enden af din **arm**.
sentence.en: Your hand is at the end of your arm.

en armbøjning.explanation: "En armbøjning" means "a push-up". It is built from "arm" (arm) and "bøjning" (bending).

sentence.da: Du laver en **armbøjning**, når du skubber kroppen op fra gulvet.
sentence.en: You do a push-up when you push your body up from the floor.

en arrangør.explanation: "En arrangør" means "an organizer". It comes from the verb "at arrangere" (to organize). To say what someone organizes, add "af" (of): "Han er arrangør af koncerten" (He is the organizer of the concert).

sentence.da: Som **arrangør** skal du finde sted, tid og frivillige til festivalen.
sentence.en: As an organizer you must find a place, a time and volunteers for the festival.

en art.explanation: "En art" means "a species". To talk about an animal that may die out, use "truet" (endangered): "Bjørnen er en truet art" (The bear is an endangered species).

sentence.da: En **art** er en gruppe dyr, der kan få unger sammen.
sentence.en: A species is a group of animals that can have young together.

en artikel.explanation: "En artikel" means "an article", as in a piece of writing. In grammar, the word also names "en" and "et": "På dansk er en og et artikler" (In Danish, en and et are articles).

sentence.da: Jeg læste en **artikel** om vores by.
sentence.en: I read an article about our city.

en arv.explanation: "En arv" means "an inheritance". When you talk about something passed down, such as traditions, use "en kulturarv" (a cultural heritage): "Eventyr er en del af vores kulturarv" (Fairy tales are part of our cultural heritage).

sentence.da: Børnene fik huset og pengene som **arv**, da deres far døde.
sentence.en: The children got the house and the money as an inheritance when their father died.

en arving.explanation: "En arving" means "an heir". It belongs to the same family as "arv" (inheritance). To talk about a royal heir, say "arving til tronen" (heir to the throne): "Prinsen er arving til tronen" (The prince is heir to the throne).

sentence.da: Som eneste **arving** fik hun både huset og alle pengene.
sentence.en: As the only heir, she got both the house and all the money.

en asiat.explanation: "En asiat" means "an Asian". Danish writes it with a small first letter: "asiat", not "Asiat". To name the person's country, use the nationality word for that country: "en thailænder" (a Thai person).

sentence.da: En **asiat** kommer fra et land i Asien, for eksempel Japan.
sentence.en: An Asian comes from a country in Asia, for example Japan.

en assistent.explanation: "En assistent" means "an assistant". Danish ends it with "-ent", not "-ant": "assistent".

sentence.da: Min **assistent** skriver mails til kunderne.
sentence.en: My assistant writes emails to the customers.

en astronaut.explanation: "En astronaut" means "an astronaut". To say what you dream of being, use "at blive" (to become): "Jeg vil gerne blive astronaut" (I would like to become an astronaut).

sentence.da: En **astronaut** rejser i en raket til månen.
sentence.en: An astronaut travels in a rocket to the moon.

en asylansøger.explanation: "En asylansøger" means "an asylum seeker". It is built from "asyl" (asylum) and "ansøger" (applicant). To say someone asks for asylum, use "at søge asyl" (to seek asylum): "Hun søger asyl i Danmark" (She is seeking asylum in Denmark).

sentence.da: Mens myndighederne undersøger sagen, er man **asylansøger**.
sentence.en: While the authorities look into the case, you are an asylum seeker.

en atmosfære.explanation: "En atmosfære" means "an atmosphere", as in the layer of gases around the Earth. When you talk about the feeling in a place, the word fits too: "Der er en god atmosfære på kontoret" (There is a good atmosphere in the office).

sentence.da: Der var en varm og rolig **atmosfære** i caféen.
sentence.en: There was a warm and calm atmosphere in the café.

en attitude.explanation: "En attitude" means "an attitude". In Danish, it means a bold, confident way of acting: "Han har attitude" (He has attitude). For a view or opinion, use "en holdning" (a stance): "Hun har en positiv holdning" (She has a positive attitude).

sentence.da: Hun går ind i rummet med **attitude** og et stort smil.
sentence.en: She walks into the room with attitude and a big smile.

en aubergine.explanation: "En aubergine" means "an eggplant". Danish uses the French spelling "aubergine", the same as British English.

sentence.da: En **aubergine** er en lilla grønsag.
sentence.en: An eggplant is a purple vegetable.

en auktion.explanation: "En auktion" means "an auction". The word is also in "et auktionshus" (an auction house): "Vi sælger billedet hos auktionshuset" (We sell the painting at the auction house).

sentence.da: Dyre malerier bliver ofte solgt på **auktion**.
sentence.en: Expensive paintings are often sold at auction.

en autograf.explanation: "En autograf" means "an autograph". Danish spells it with "f", not "ph": "autograf". To ask a famous person for one, say "Må jeg få en autograf?" (May I have an autograph?)

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **autograf** af min yndlingssanger.
sentence.en: I got an autograph from my favorite singer.

en autoritet.explanation: "En autoritet" means "an authority". To say someone is trusted because of what they know, use "på området" (in the field): "Hun er en autoritet på området" (She is an authority in the field). For government offices, use "myndighederne" (the authorities): "Myndighederne undersøger sagen" (The authorities are looking into the case).

sentence.da: En lærer er en **autoritet** i klassen.
sentence.en: A teacher is an authority in the class.

en autostol.explanation: "En autostol" means "a car seat". It is built from "auto" (car) and "stol" (chair).

sentence.da: Barnet skal sidde i en **autostol** i bilen.
sentence.en: The child has to sit in a car seat in the car.

en avis.explanation: "En avis" means "a newspaper". To say you have a regular delivery that you pay for, use "abonnere på" (to subscribe to): "Vi abonnerer på en avis" (We subscribe to a newspaper).

sentence.da: Min far læser en **avis** hver morgen.
sentence.en: My dad reads a newspaper every morning.

en avocado.explanation: "En avocado" means "an avocado". To say it is ripe, use "moden" (ripe): "Avocadoen er moden" (The avocado is ripe).

sentence.da: Guacamole er lavet af **avocado**.
sentence.en: Guacamole is made of avocado.

et abonnement.explanation: "Et abonnement" means "a subscription". To say you start one, use "tegne" (to take out): "Jeg vil gerne tegne et abonnement" (I would like to take out a subscription).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler hver måned for mit **abonnement**.
sentence.en: I pay for my subscription every month.

et adgangskrav.explanation: "Et adgangskrav" means "an admission requirement". It is built from "adgang" (access) and "krav" (demand). To say you meet it, use "opfylde" (to fulfil): "Hun opfylder adgangskravet" (She meets the admission requirement).

sentence.da: Studiet har et **adgangskrav**: mindst 7 i dansk.
sentence.en: The program has an admission requirement: at least a 7 in Danish.

et afslag.explanation: "Et afslag" means "a refusal". When you talk about a lower price, it means "a price reduction": "Vi fik et afslag i prisen" (We got a reduction in the price).

sentence.da: Hun fik et **afslag** på sin ansøgning om støtte.
sentence.en: She got a refusal on her application for support.

et afsnit.explanation: "Et afsnit" means "an episode". When you count what you watched, say: "Jeg har set tre afsnit" (I have watched three episodes). When you talk about a text, it means "a section": "Læs det første afsnit" (Read the first section).

sentence.da: Vi så det sidste **afsnit** i går aftes.
sentence.en: We watched the last episode last night.

et agern.explanation: "Et agern" means "an acorn". Do not mix it up with "et egern" (a squirrel). To say an acorn lies somewhere: "Der ligger et agern på jorden" (There is an acorn on the ground). To say a squirrel is somewhere: "Der sidder et egern i træet" (There is a squirrel in the tree).

sentence.da: Et **agern** er frøet fra et egetræ.
sentence.en: An acorn is the seed from an oak tree.

et aktieselskab.explanation: "Et aktieselskab" means "a public limited company". It is built from "aktie" (share) and "selskab" (company). In a company name, the short form is "A/S": "Carlsberg A/S".

sentence.da: Ejerne af et **aktieselskab** har hver købt en del af firmaet.
sentence.en: The owners of a public limited company have each bought a part of the firm.

et akvarium.explanation: "Et akvarium" means "an aquarium". When you talk about a place you visit with many large tanks, it also means "an aquarium": "Vi så hajer i akvariet" (We saw sharks in the aquarium).

sentence.da: Børnene kan se fisk i et stort **akvarium**.
sentence.en: The children can see fish in a big aquarium.

et alarmnummer.explanation: "Et alarmnummer" means "an emergency number". It is built from "alarm" (alarm) and "nummer" (number).

sentence.da: Du kan ringe til **alarmnummer** 112.
sentence.en: You can call the emergency number 112.

et album.explanation: "Et album" means "an album". To talk about photos, put "foto" (photo) in front: "et fotoalbum" (a photo album).

sentence.da: Bandet har lavet et nyt **album**.
sentence.en: The band has made a new album.

et alfabet.explanation: "Et alfabet" means "an alphabet". A fact about Denmark: the Danish alphabet has 29 letters. To say things are in alphabetical order, use "alfabetisk" (alphabetical): "Ordene står i alfabetisk rækkefølge" (The words are in alphabetical order).

sentence.da: Æ, ø og å kommer sidst i det danske **alfabet**.
sentence.en: Æ, ø and å come last in the Danish alphabet.

et alibi.explanation: "Et alibi" means "an alibi". When you talk about an excuse, it also means "an excuse": "Hun brugte travlheden som alibi" (She used being busy as an excuse).

sentence.da: Han havde et **alibi**, for han var i udlandet den aften.
sentence.en: He had an alibi, because he was abroad that evening.

et alternativ.explanation: "Et alternativ" means "an alternative". To say there is no other choice, say: "Der er intet alternativ" (There is no alternative). When you describe something as different from the normal kind, it works as an adjective: "alternativ medicin" (alternative medicine).

sentence.da: Cyklen er et godt **alternativ** til bussen.
sentence.en: The bike is a good alternative to the bus.

et anførselstegn.explanation: "Et anførselstegn" means "a quotation mark". It is also called "gåseøjne" (literally, goose eyes). To say you put a word between quotation marks, say: "Skriv ordet i anførselstegn" (Write the word in quotation marks).

sentence.da: Et citat står mellem to **anførselstegn**.
sentence.en: A quote stands between two quotation marks.

et angreb.explanation: "Et angreb" means "an attack". It comes from the verb "at angribe" (to attack). To say someone starts attacking, use "gå til angreb" (to go on the attack): "Soldaterne gik til angreb" (The soldiers went on the attack).

sentence.da: Holdet sætter et hurtigt **angreb** ind mod målet.
sentence.en: The team launches a fast attack toward the goal.

et anker.explanation: "Et anker" means "an anchor". To say a ship pulls up its anchor and leaves, use "lette anker" (to weigh anchor): "Skibet letter anker" (The ship weighs anchor).

sentence.da: Kaptajnen kaster **anker** uden for havnen.
sentence.en: The captain drops anchor outside the harbor.

et anlæg.explanation: "Et anlæg" means "a facility or plant". To name a specific kind of facility, put a word in front: "et idrætsanlæg" (a sports facility).

sentence.da: Vandet bliver renset på et **anlæg** uden for byen.
sentence.en: The water is cleaned at a facility outside the town.

et anpartsselskab.explanation: "Et anpartsselskab" means "a private limited company". It is built from "anpart" (share) and "selskab" (company). In a company name, the short form is "ApS": "Café Sol ApS".

sentence.da: Hun valgte et **anpartsselskab**, fordi hun ikke vil hæfte personligt for gæld.
sentence.en: She chose a private limited company because she does not want to be personally liable for debt.

et ansigt.explanation: "Et ansigt" means "a face". To say people meet in person, use "ansigt til ansigt" (face to face): "Vi mødtes ansigt til ansigt" (We met face to face).

sentence.da: Øjne og næse sidder i dit **ansigt**.
sentence.en: Eyes and nose are in your face.

et ansigtstræk.explanation: "Et ansigtstræk" means "a facial feature". Do not mix it up with "et ansigtsudtryk" (a facial expression). To talk about a part of the face, use "ansigtstræk": "Hans næse er et tydeligt ansigtstræk" (His nose is a clear facial feature). To talk about the look on a face, use "ansigtsudtryk": "Hun fik et vredt ansigtsudtryk" (She got an angry facial expression).

sentence.da: Hans bløde **ansigtstræk** ligner hans fars.
sentence.en: His soft facial features look like his father's.

et ansigtsudtryk.explanation: "Et ansigtsudtryk" means "a facial expression". To say what the expression is like, put a describing word in front: "et glad ansigtsudtryk" (a happy facial expression).

sentence.da: Hendes **ansigtsudtryk** viste, at hun var meget overrasket.
sentence.en: Her facial expression showed that she was very surprised.

et ansvar.explanation: "Et ansvar" means "a responsibility". To say someone accepts it, use "tage" (to take): "Han tager ansvar for fejlen" (He takes responsibility for the mistake).

sentence.da: Du har et stort **ansvar** på arbejdet.
sentence.en: You have a big responsibility at work.

et antal.explanation: "Et antal" means "a number (amount)", as in how many. When you talk about how many guests came, say: "Antallet af gæster var lille" (The number of guests was small). Do not mix it up with "et tal" (a number). When you talk about the number 5 itself, use "et tal": "Fem er et tal" (Five is a number).

sentence.da: Et stort **antal** mennesker kom til festen.
sentence.en: A large number of people came to the party.

et apotek.explanation: "Et apotek" means "a pharmacy". To say where you are going, use "på" (at): "Jeg skal på apoteket" (I have to go to the pharmacy).

sentence.da: Jeg køber medicin på et **apotek**.
sentence.en: I buy medicine at a pharmacy.

et apparat.explanation: "Et apparat" means "a device". To name a specific kind of device, put a word in front: "et høreapparat" (a hearing aid).

sentence.da: Det nye **apparat** i køkkenet er meget let at bruge.
sentence.en: The new appliance in the kitchen is very easy to use.

et ar.explanation: "Et ar" means "a scar". Do not mix it up with "et år" (a year), which has a little ring over the "å". To talk about a scar: "Såret blev til et ar" (The wound became a scar). To talk about a year: "Et år har tolv måneder" (A year has twelve months).

sentence.da: Han har et **ar** på kinden efter en gammel skade.
sentence.en: He has a scar on his cheek from an old injury.

et arbejde.explanation: "Et arbejde" means "a job or work". To say you are at your workplace, use "på arbejde" (at work): "Jeg er på arbejde" (I am at work).

sentence.da: Jeg skal på **arbejde** nu.
sentence.en: I have to go to work now.

et arbejdsmiljø.explanation: "Et arbejdsmiljø" means "a work environment". It is built from "arbejde" (work) and "miljø" (environment). In Denmark, "Arbejdstilsynet" (the Danish Working Environment Authority) is the authority that checks the work environment.

sentence.da: Et godt **arbejdsmiljø** betyder, at man trives på jobbet.
sentence.en: A good work environment means that people feel good at work.

et areal.explanation: "Et areal" means "an area", as in the size of a surface. To ask how big a room is, say: "Hvad er rummets areal?" (What is the area of the room?) Do not mix it up with "et område" (an area as a region). To talk about a region, say: "Der er mange parker i området" (There are many parks in the area).

sentence.da: Haven har et **areal** på tre hundrede kvadratmeter.
sentence.en: The garden has an area of three hundred square meters.

et argument.explanation: "Et argument" means "an argument", as in a reason for your view. To ask for someone's reason, say: "Hvad er dit argument?" (What is your argument?) Do not mix it up with "et skænderi" (a quarrel). To say two people had a quarrel: "De havde et skænderi i går" (They had a quarrel yesterday).

sentence.da: Jeg har et godt **argument** for at blive hjemme.
sentence.en: I have a good argument for staying home.

et arkiv.explanation: "Et arkiv" means "an archive". To name what is stored, put a word in front: "et fotoarkiv" (a photo archive).

sentence.da: Byens gamle billeder ligger i et **arkiv**.
sentence.en: The town's old pictures are kept in an archive.

et armbånd.explanation: "Et armbånd" means "a bracelet". It is built from arm (arm) and bånd (band), the same bånd as in "et hårbånd" (a hair band).

sentence.da: Hun har et pænt **armbånd** om håndleddet.
sentence.en: She has a pretty bracelet around her wrist.

et armbåndsur.explanation: "Et armbåndsur" means "a wristwatch". It is built from "armbånd" (bracelet) and "ur" (watch or clock).

sentence.da: Et **armbåndsur** bærer man om håndleddet.
sentence.en: You wear a wristwatch around the wrist.

et askebæger.explanation: "Et askebæger" means "an ashtray". It ends in "bæger" (cup), as in "et æggebæger" (an egg cup).

sentence.da: Hun lægger cigaretten i et **askebæger**.
sentence.en: She puts the cigarette in an ashtray.

et aspekt.explanation: "Et aspekt" means "an aspect". To say which part matters most, say: "Det vigtigste aspekt er prisen" (The most important aspect is the price).

sentence.da: Prisen er kun ét **aspekt** af beslutningen.
sentence.en: The price is only one aspect of the decision.

et atom.explanation: "Et atom" means "an atom". It is the first part of "atomkraft" (nuclear power) and "atombombe" (atomic bomb).

sentence.da: Et **atom** er så lille, at man ikke kan se det.
sentence.en: An atom is so small that you cannot see it.

et auditorium.explanation: "Et auditorium" means "an auditorium or lecture hall". To say where you meet for a lecture: "Vi mødes i auditoriet" (We meet in the lecture hall).

sentence.da: I et **auditorium** sidder mange studerende og lytter til en underviser.
sentence.en: In a lecture hall, many students sit and listen to a teacher.

et autoværksted.explanation: "Et autoværksted" means "a car repair shop". It is built from "auto" (car) and "værksted" (workshop), which also appears in "et cykelværksted" (a bike repair shop).

sentence.da: Bilen er i stykker, og jeg skal til et **autoværksted**.
sentence.en: The car is broken, and I have to go to a car repair shop.
